Title: Rural allocation issue won't strain PH-BN ties, says PKR Youth chief
Article:
LUMUT: Differences of opinion over Rural and Regional Development Ministry allocations under the Finance Ministry will not affect Pakatan Harapan-Barisan Nasional political ties.
PKR Youth chief Muhammad Kamil Abdul Munim said differing approaches were normal in political cooperation and had been managed well in previous elections.
"There is no issue about it being affected. Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has suggested that the issue between the ministries be coordinated harmoniously through internal discussions," he said after officiating an event at the Teluk Batik Campsite here today.
Kamil, who is political secretary to the finance minister, said Finance Ministry-level discussions will review allocation requirements and prioritise high-impact rural development projects.
The issue arose following differing statements from PH and BN leaders regarding allocations for rural development projects, raising speculation about coalition harmony ahead of the Melaka election.
It followed remarks by Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi, who is also Rural and Regional Development Minister, concerning payment delays for contractors handling projects under his ministry.
On Wednesday (Sept 2), Treasury Secretary-General Tan Sri Johan Mahmood Merican clarified that there were no restrictions on the ministry's allocations for rural road projects, adding that constraints in contractor payments occurred because the current year's allocation had been nearly fully spent.
In a separate development, Kamil described Kepong member of parliament Lim Lip Eng's proposal for the government to consider reintroducing the Goods and Services Tax (GST) as a personal opinion based on his own analysis.
He said the government's stance remains to continue implementing the Sales and Services Tax (SST), though policies may evolve according to changing economic needs.
"For now, the government's decision is to proceed with the existing policy," he added.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Zahid gives Rauf mandate to negotiate BN's Melaka election partnerships
Article:
MELAKA: Barisan Nasional (BN) chairman Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi has given Chief Minister Datuk Seri Ab Rauf Yusoh the mandate to negotiate cooperation with any party for the upcoming Melaka state election.
Zahid said any chosen partner must be sincere and honest to ensure BN continues to lead the state administration in the next term.
"Datuk Rauf, I give you the mandate to negotiate well. Choose a loyal partner, one that can deliver victory for us.
"Choose a partner who is sincere and honest with us, one who speaks the same behind our backs as to our face, not a partner who says one thing in front and does another behind our back," he said.
Zahid said this at the closing ceremony of the Melaka Youth Carnival 2026, which was also attended by Ab Rauf, at the Melaka International Trade Centre (MITC) parking grounds in Ayer Keroh here today.
He also reminded Melaka BN to defend the 21 state seats won by the coalition in the previous election.
In the 2021 Melaka state election, BN won 21 seats, while Pakatan Harapan (PH) won 5 and Perikatan Nasional (PN) secured 2.
The current term of the Melaka State Assembly ends this December.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Trump envoys arrive in Kyiv for first Ukraine visit
Article:
KYIV: US envoys Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff arrived in Kyiv Sunday for their first visit to the Ukrainian capital, a day after holding talks with Russia's Vladimir Putin in the Kremlin on ending more than four years of war between the neighbours.
US President Donald Trump's business partner Witkoff and son-in-law Kushner had visited Moscow several times but had not held talks in Kyiv – hit by deadly Russian strikes since 2022.
They are due to meet with Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy. An AFP reporter in Kyiv saw the American envoys arrive by train.
They are hoping to revive negotiations to end Europe's worst conflict since WWII, after a summer of escalation.
Moscow's invasion of Ukraine has killed hundreds of thousands of people and displaced millions.
Witkoff and Kushner met with Putin on Saturday to "advance President Trump's agenda of peace in the Russia-Ukraine War," a White House official said in a statement to AFP.
"The two sides discussed substantive plans for next steps, which will be announced in the coming weeks, and look forward to equally productive meetings tomorrow in Ukraine."
Kremlin aide Yuri Ushakov called the talks "extremely frank", saying the Americans "put forward a number of ideas on possible routes to a settlement", but did not elaborate.
The Russian side told the Americans that Moscow was "confident" it could achieve its military goals of seizing the rest of eastern Ukraine, Ushakov added.
Both Russia and Ukraine have vowed not to strike each other's capitals for three days to allow for the negotiations to take place.
It was Kushner and Witkoff's eighth visit to Moscow during the war – but it is their first in the Ukrainian capital, hit by deadly Russian strikes throughout the war.
Russia's TASS news agency reported early Sunday that Witkoff and Kushner had arrived in Rzeszow in Poland on their way to Kyiv.
Zelenskyy on Sunday said Ukraine was "ready for the conversation."
"Ukraine has always been and will remain constructive," the wartime leader said on social media ahead of their visit.
The country's airspace has been closed since Moscow launched the war in February 2022 and visiting leaders have been arriving by train.
For many Ukrainians, hopes of a breakthrough remain slim.
"At this point it doesn't give me any hope. There have already been too many negotiations," Yaroslav, a 29-year-old Kyiv resident, told AFP.
PUTIN THANKS TRUMP
In televised comments before the talks, Putin said Russia would ensure the safety of the envoys in Kyiv – a city Moscow has pounded with deadly strikes throughout the war.
"We will do everything that depends on us to ensure the safety of the negotiation process and mediators such as yourselves," Putin told Witkoff and Kushner.
Earlier Saturday, Putin had thanked Trump for persisting in his efforts to end the war despite it being "not simple."
Of the envoys' trip to Kyiv, he said: "No matter what happens next, contacts of this kind are undoubtedly always beneficial."
Trump said on Friday his envoys were bringing a "proposal" to end fighting.
"We have an idea for peace," he said, without elaborating.
US efforts have so far not led to a breakthrough in the war, and peace efforts have stalled in part because of Washington's war with Iran.
Russia occupied large swathes of eastern and southern Ukraine, and Putin has insisted Moscow is intent on seizing the rest of eastern Ukraine.
LIMITED TRUCE
Both Moscow and Kyiv committed to suspending strikes as the negotiations took place.
"The Russian president, the commander-in-chief, has given the order from midnight not to strike Kyiv for three days," Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said.
Zelenskyy said he had spoken to the US envoys and also promised Kyiv would not strike Moscow.
"From now through the end of Saturday, as well as on Sunday and Monday, Ukraine is ready to refrain from strikes on Moscow," Zelenskyy said.
But fighting continued elsewhere. Ukraine's air force said Russia attacked overnight with 108 drones and missiles, while Moscow said it had shot down 258 drones.
On Saturday, Putin said he had "noted that the Ukrainian side significantly reduced" its strikes on Russia and Moscow.
However, Kyiv said that Russian strikes had killed 10 people across the country Saturday – including a child and his family members in the Kharkiv region and two people outside Kyiv.

Title: Study causes of Old Klang Road jams before building flyover, says expert
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: A transport policy expert has urged Kuala Lumpur City Hall (DBKL) and the Public Works Department (PWD) to diagnose the causes of congestion along Old Klang Road before deciding whether to build a proposed double-decker road or flyover.
MY Mobility Vision founder and senior adviser Wan Agyl Wan Hassan was responding to Seputeh member of parliament Teresa Kok's call for DBKL and PWD to study the need for additional road capacity along the busy Kuala Lumpur corridor.
Kok, in a Facebook post, had also urged DBKL to study worsening congestion in Bukit Jalil and Sri Petaling, particularly amid concerns over high-density development and inadequate public transport access.
Wan Agyl said Kok's call for a study was reasonable, but stressed that authorities should first identify what was causing the congestion and which solutions would remain effective in the longer term.
"Before DBKL and PWD start with the structure, they should start with the problem."What is actually causing the congestion? Which parts of the corridor are failing? And more importantly, which intervention will still work five or 10 years after it is built?" he said in a statement.
Wan Agyl said adding road capacity did not necessarily provide lasting relief, as faster journeys could attract more motorists to the route — a phenomenon known as induced demand.
However, he said a flyover could be effective if traffic modelling showed that specific junctions or conflicts between through and local traffic were causing major delays.
"Every vehicle entering an elevated road has to come down somewhere. If the next junction, merge or connecting road is already congested, we have not solved the problem. We have shifted it," he said.
He called for a comprehensive corridor mobility study covering traffic flows, major bottlenecks, local and through-traffic, public transport, parking and loading activity, as well as traffic generated by future developments.
Wan Agyl said authorities should also focus on how many people, rather than vehicles, could be moved by each intervention.
"If one project allows another 2,000 cars through a corridor, while another allows several thousand more people to travel reliably by bus, which one creates more transport capacity?" he said.
He said possible solutions should include junction improvements, traffic signal optimisation, access management, parking enforcement, improved bus services and feeder routes, with a flyover considered if supported by the evidence.
Wan Agyl also said high-density development and transport planning must be considered together, as poor public transport, walking links and feeder services could increase car dependency.
"Density itself is not the enemy. Dense development can support good public transport," he said.
He said Old Klang Road offered DBKL an opportunity to apply the principles of the Kuala Lumpur Structure Plan 2040, particularly on accessibility, efficient mobility and integrating development with public transport.
"The important thing is to diagnose first and prescribe second."If the evidence says the flyover is the best answer, build it. If the evidence points elsewhere, we should have the discipline to choose the better option," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Man suspected of drug activities shot dead in Seremban
Article:
SEREMBAN: A man suspected of involvement in drug-related activities was shot dead in a residential area in Garden Homes here early this afternoon.
Negri Sembilan police chief Datuk Alzafny Ahmad said the incident occurred at 1.50pm.
Further details will be disclosed by the Bukit Aman Narcotics Crime Investigation Department director at the Seremban District Police Headquarters tomorrow.
"Yes, I confirm the incident," he told reporters here today.
The suspect, believed to be in his 50s, had eight previous records for drug and criminal offences and was wanted in connection with a case under the Kidnapping Act.
A resident, who wanted to be known only as Ali, 72, said he was at home after prayers when a neighbour informed him about the incident.
He said the neighbour reported hearing what sounded like several gunshots, although he did not hear them himself as he was indoors.
"After that, I saw many patrol cars and the road leading to the scene was cordoned off with police tape, with vehicles barred from entering.
"This is the first time such an incident has occurred in this residential area. We are concerned about our safety should a similar incident happen again," he said.
The senior citizen added that residents had noticed several suspicious cars parked near the area around midnight about a week ago.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: [UPDATED] Former Felda-linked body general manager among two arrested over land irregularities
Article:
PUTRAJAYA: A former general manager of a statutory body linked to the Federal Land Development Authority (Felda), who holds the title Datuk, is one of two people arrested by the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) over alleged irregularities involving the sale of land belonging to the statutory body.
Both men, aged in their 50s and 60s, were arrested at about 4pm today after they were called to the MACC headquarters here to have their statements recorded.
They are suspected of being involved in alleged misappropriation, abuse of power and corruption in the appointment of a developer for a project in Kuala Lumpur.
The duo are also suspected of involvement in the sale of land belonging to the statutory body to a company with interests linked to the developer, allegedly without the knowledge of the body's board of directors and its subsidiary.
Both suspects will be brought before the magistrate's court here tomorrow for remand.
MACC chief commissioner Datuk Seri Abd Halim Aman, when contacted, confirmed the arrests.
He said the case was being investigated under Section 16 of the MACC Act 2009, which covers offences involving the soliciting, receiving, offering or giving of gratification as an inducement or reward in connection with a transaction or matter.
An offence under Section 16 is punishable under Section 24 of the same Act by imprisonment of up to 20 years and a fine of not less than five times the value of the gratification involved, or RM10,000, whichever is higher, upon conviction.
Earlier today, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said issues involving a
Felda subsidiary
would be exposed within the next few weeks.
He said the disclosure was aimed at identifying weaknesses within the institution.
Abd Halim was previously quoted as saying that he did not rule out the possibility of several individuals being detained in stages starting this week.
This followed allegations of misappropriation, abuse of power and corruption involving a Felda subsidiary.
He had said that, so far, 12 people had been called to assist in investigations into the case.
It was reported that seven Felda-related cases previously investigated or highlighted in forensic reports had been reopened after new information emerged, the MACC said.
The new leads provided grounds for the commission to re-examine the cases.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Gerakan Youth urges party to draw clear line against extremism
Article:
GEORGE TOWN: Gerakan Youth has urged the party not to compromise with extremism, warning that doing so could further erode support among moderate voters.
Speaking at the party's delegates' conference, Penang Gerakan Youth chief Tan Zhen Zune said Gerakan could work with any party, but must maintain its principles and draw a clear line against extremism.
He said Gerakan needed partners that were moderate, multiracial, respected the Federal Constitution and upheld the rights of all Malaysians.
"Cooperation should complement each other and seek common ground. But cooperation cannot come at the cost of losing our own principles," he said.
Tan said Gerakan also could not afford to be associated with extremist views, particularly when racial and religious issues were repeatedly raised by parties within Perikatan Nasional.
He questioned whether PN was sufficiently focused on issues affecting Malaysians' daily lives, including raising incomes, creating better jobs, assisting small and medium enterprises, retaining talent and helping young people own homes.
"If a party constantly talks about race and religion, but the people are unclear about its economic plans, surely they will ask: 'Besides race and religion, what else can PN do for our country?'" he said.
Tan said Gerakan was currently "caught in the middle", with Malay voters having larger and stronger Malay-based parties with wider grassroots networks, while non-Malay voters were increasingly finding it difficult to accept Gerakan.
He said Gerakan leaders were often left explaining or defending controversial statements made by coalition partners, while sometimes choosing to remain silent.
"The result? We have yet to truly gain Malay support, while non-Malay support is increasingly slipping away," he added.
Tan questioned Gerakan's position within PN, asking whether the party was genuinely treated as a partner or merely used to demonstrate that the coalition was multiracial.
"When it comes to policies, direction, seat allocations and major decisions, we have to honestly ask: 'To what extent is Gerakan's voice actually heard?'" he said.
He also questioned how many of Gerakan's original supporters remained with the party, how much Malay support it had actually gained, and how many moderate voters and grassroots members had been lost.
Tan said the party must also consider whether its supporters would remain loyal to Gerakan if its coalition partners no longer needed it.
"Gerakan can cooperate with anyone. But we must have principles. We must have a line," he said.
He warned that failing to address extremist statements and allowing overly conservative and extreme thinking to affect the rights of Malaysians would ultimately come at Gerakan's expense.
Tan later announced that he was stepping down as Penang Gerakan Youth chief and Gerakan Youth deputy secretary-general, saying he could no longer continue along a political path he did not believe in.
He said he had previously hoped to change the party's direction and had tried to do so, but eventually realised he was unable to bring about the change he wanted.
"I cannot continue forcing myself to accept a path that I myself do not believe in. And I cannot ask my fellow youth members to believe in something that I myself cannot convince myself of," he said.
Tan said he would submit his formal resignation letter to the Gerakan Youth secretary-general.
He apologised to delegates who might be disappointed by his decision, but said he had to remain true to his principles and take responsibility for what he believed in.
He expressed hope that Gerakan could rediscover its identity and direction before it was too late and return to being a party that genuinely represented all Malaysians.
"That is why, for me, Gerakan still needs to exist," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: US interference claim: 'One side may be lying' – Kamil Munim
Article:
LUMUT: PKR Youth has urged authorities to investigate a claim by Pas president Tan Sri Abdul Hadi Awang that the United States had offered assistance to the party to topple the Barisan Nasional government under former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak.
Its chief Muhammad Kamil Abdul Munim said the contradiction between Hadi's claim and the US Embassy's denial showed the matter was serious and warranted an investigation.
"One side may be lying, and this should be investigated by the authorities.
"Following this disclosure, we urge the authorities to launch an investigation to determine whether the claim is true," he said after officiating the closing ceremony of the Malaysian Silat Seni Gayong Association's event today.
Kamil, who is also the political secretary to the finance minister, said that if true, immediate action must be taken as the matter involved an attempt to use a foreign power to undermine the government and parliamentary democracy.
"If it is true, immediate action must be taken. We cannot allow any party to directly use an external power to undermine the system.
"An attempt to topple the government is a serious offence that cannot be taken lightly," he said.
Hadi, during his winding-up speech at the 72nd Pas Annual Muktamar yesterday,
claimed
that a representative of the US Embassy once asked him about the party's proposed candidate for prime minister during a meeting at the embassy here.
Hadi said the question was raised after two senior Pas leaders, Datuk Seri Takiyuddin Hassan and Datuk Dr Ahmad Samsuri Mokhtar, had earlier met the US ambassador.
Hadi said the meeting took place when Pas was still part of the Pakatan Rakyat coalition, during the visit of US President Barack Obama to Malaysia.
Earlier today, the US Embassy in Kuala Lumpur
denied
ever seeking to determine Malaysia's political leadership, calling any suggestion otherwise false.
"The US has never sought to decide Malaysia's political leadership. Any account to the contrary is false," US Chargé d'Affaires David H. Gamble Jr said in a statement.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Air quality deteriorates, 35 areas record unhealthy API readings
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Air quality deteriorated across several parts of the country this evening, with 35 monitoring stations recording unhealthy or very unhealthy Air Pollutant Index (API) readings as of 5pm today.
Data released by the Department of Environment (DoE) on Facebook showed that one station recorded a very unhealthy API reading, while another 34 stations were classified as unhealthy.
Sri Aman, Sarawak, recorded the country's highest API reading at 214, placing it in the very unhealthy category.
Among stations recording unhealthy readings, Samarahan registered an API of 196, followed by Samalaju (194), Bintulu (189), Mukah (188) and Kuching (188).
Other areas with unhealthy air quality included Sarikei (184), PPD Serian (184), Johan Setia in Selangor (180), ILP Miri (175), Sibu (173), Miri (169) and Shah Alam (168).
The DoE data also showed that Putrajaya recorded an API of 162, while Jerantut, Pahang, recorded 168.
Overall, 29 stations recorded moderate air quality, while three stations recorded good air quality. No station was classified as having hazardous air quality.
The API classifies readings of 101 to 200 as unhealthy, 201 to 300 as very unhealthy and above 300 as hazardous.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: UiTM student's death during endurance challenge: Lab analysis pending
Article:
MARAN: The post-mortem findings on the death of a Universiti Teknologi Mara (UiTM) student who collapsed at the UiTM Jengka campus on Sept 4 are pending laboratory analysis.
Fadhlan Fakhry Solana Mohd Fellimal, 21,
died at the Sultan Haji Ahmad Shah Hospital (Hoshas)
in Temerloh at 2.08pm yesterday.
Maran police chief Superintendent Wong Kim Wai said the victim, who was from UiTM Seremban, Negri Sembilan, was taken to Jengka Hospital with eight other participants after experiencing
breathing difficulties
at 9.57pm.
"The student was in serious condition due to a severe drop in oxygen levels and was referred to Hoshas. He died at 2.08pm.
"The case is still under investigation. We are awaiting the full reports from the Chemistry Department," he said in a statement today.
He said of the remaining eight participants, two were warded in the ICU at Hoshas yesterday, while six others were receiving treatment at Jengka Hospital. All were in stable condition.
Fadhlan Fakhry was participating in the Komander Kesatria Endurance Challenge duathlon when he experienced breathing difficulties with the eight other participants, including four women.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Police open two probes after toddler mauled by five stray dogs
Article:
BATU PAHAT: Police have opened two investigation papers after a 2-year-old girl was
severely injured
in an attack by five stray dogs at Kampung Tambak in Peserai here yesterday.
District police chief Assistant Commissioner Shahrulanuar Mushaddat Abdullah Sani said investigations are being conducted under Section 31(1)(a) of the Child Act 2001 for child neglect and Section 289 of the Penal Code for negligence with respect to animals.
He said the investigation was initiated after police received a report from the hospital regarding a child undergoing treatment for severe injuries.
"Preliminary investigations by the district Criminal Investigation Department found the incident occurred at 7am yesterday in front of the victim's family home in Peserai.
"The victim, a girl aged 2 years and 10 months, was outside the house when she was attacked by a pack of stray dogs.
"The attack left her with injuries across almost her entire body. She was initially taken by family members to Sultanah Nora Ismail Hospital (HSNI) in Batu Pahat for treatment before being transferred to Sultanah Aminah Hospital (HSA) in Johor Baru for further care," he said.
Shahrulanuar added that the victim is currently in stable condition and police investigations into the incident are ongoing.
In the incident, Nur Haira Watikah Mohammad Hamizi was found lying on the ground with severe wounds to her head and face.
Her parents had dropped her off at the home of her grandmother, Darlinda Darlis, 56, for the school holidays, where her older brother and sister were also staying.
The grandmother realised the child was missing after noticing the sliding front door was slightly open.
She went outside to look for her and found five dogs surrounding the child, who was covered in blood.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: [UPDATED] Zahid says "blue wave" will recur in upcoming Melaka  polls
Article:
AYER KEROH: The "blue wave" phenomenon, intensified by the political understanding between Barisan Nasional and Perikatan Nasional that previously swept the Johor and Negri Sembilan polls, could be repeated in the upcoming Melaka election, Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi said.
The BN chairman, who is also Umno president, said this was based on the support of young people and Melaka voters as a whole, whom he described as being in the mood for a blue wave.
"When the big day (Melaka polling day) arrives to determine the future of Melaka, do not forget that the blue wave that happened in Johor and Negri Sembilan will also reach Melaka," he said when closing the Melaka Youth Carnival X Jom Heboh at the Melaka International Trade Centre (MITC) here today.
Also present was Chief Minister Datuk Seri Ab Rauf Yusoh.
Zahid, who is also the deputy prime minister, said BN is leaving it to Ab Rauf, who is Melaka BN chairman, to negotiate with any coalition interested in partnering with BN for the state polls.
"Datuk Seri Rauf, I give you the mandate to negotiate well. Choose a loyal partner, a partner that can give us victory, a partner that is sincere and honest with us, and a partner that speaks the same behind our backs as they do in front of us.
"Negotiate well and take care of the hearts of the people of Melaka. Do not win fewer than 21 seats. As for the remaining seven seats, it is fine to leave them to our partners," he said.
He reminded negotiators to prioritise the interests of Melaka residents and ensure BN's strength is maintained.
Zahid, who is also Umno president, called on Ab Rauf not to delay the dissolution of the Melaka State Legislative Assembly.
"Use the support from these young people to continue stabilising Melaka politics. Give them an opportunity.
"Announce the dissolution quickly. Do not wait too long; the sooner, the better because the youth are ready," he said.
Addressing internal discussions regarding potential political pacts, Zahid urged the people to remain confident in the upcoming decisions.
"I saw Dr Akmal (Datuk Dr Muhamad Akmal Saleh) offering not to contest if we partner with the other side, but do not worry, Dr Akmal, I know what will happen.
"I know whose voice the young people of Melaka want to hear. I know who the Melaka voters want us to cooperate with. When the time comes, I will make the best decision for Melaka," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: After heatwaves, will EU pivot back to the climate fight?
Article:
IS climate change set for a comeback as a top EU priority, after a deadly summer of record-breaking heatwaves across Europe?
The fight against global warming is expected to feature prominently in a key policy speech by EU chief Ursula von der Leyen this month, after two years critics say were marked by major environmental rollbacks.
With Europe barely emerging from a sweltering summer, climate would have been hard to ignore in the normally sprawling "State of the European Union" address – a yearly speech setting out political priorities for the next 12 months.
After years as a leading EU cause, climate concerns have taken the backseat to defence and industry goals over the past couple of years – to the frustration of environmentalists.
The bloc has notably watered down new green rules for businesses and proposed abandoning a ban on the sale of new internal combustion engine cars by 2035.
Yet some hope the Sept 16 speech could signal a rebalancing of priorities in Brussels.
In August, about 200 environmental groups urged von der Leyen in a letter to use the speech to lay out concrete plans to wean the 27-nation bloc off fossil fuels.
And in a possible harbinger of things to come, the EU's 27 commissioners are scheduled to meet Swedish climatologist Johan Rockstrom for a post-summer seminar in Brussels on Friday.
But other evidence points in a different direction.
EU sources say von der Leyen will focus on "climate resilience" and the economic potential of green industries – two low-hanging fruits.
The latter has been a familiar refrain during von der Leyen's seven years at the helm and legislation on climate resilience was already due to be presented before the end of the year.
The kind of ambitious climate legislation that defined von der Leyen's first five years in office – known as the Green Deal – is a hard sell in Brussels these days.
Green parties lost out in the 2024 European elections, and the business-friendly centre-right now holds sway in a European Parliament where climate sceptics on the far-right also have a bigger say.
The priority is not "to repaint in green laws that Europeans have asked to be changed", said right-wing lawmaker Celine Imart.
Within the commission itself there are divisions.
In recent months for example green voices have clashed with pro-business colleagues over the impact of a carbon market reform on the aviation and maritime transport sectors.
At the same time, EU countries are wrangling over where to allocate the limited resources that are to be dished out under the bloc's next long-term budget.
"It's going to be an uphill battle," said Green leader Terry Reintke.
Her group was nevertheless going to "push very, very hard" to have von der Leyen lay out concrete climate actions in her speech.
"We are talking about existential situations here," she told AFP.
* The writer is from AFP
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Selangor to close schools if API exceeds 200 as haze worsens
Article:
SHAH ALAM: Selangor will close schools, kindergartens, and childcare centres if the Air Pollutant Index (API) reading exceeds 200, according to state authorities.
State Public Health and Environment Committee chairman Jamaliah Jamaluddin said the Selangor Education Department will continue to monitor API readings at school locations and take appropriate action based on pollution levels.
"For the education sector, schools, kindergartens, and childcare centres must comply with prevailing regulations based on API readings.
"If the API reading exceeds 200, the closure of schools, kindergartens, and childcare centres will be implemented according to set directives. School authorities must also ensure student safety and health remain the top priority throughout the haze period," she said in a statement today.
Jamaliah said the state government is strengthening agency preparedness following an uptick in API readings across several areas in Selangor since this morning.
As of 11am, six areas recorded unhealthy API levels: Johan Setia (180), Shah Alam (168), Petaling Jaya (157), Klang (155), Banting (155), and Kuala Selangor (155).
"Open burning is strictly prohibited. Firm action will be taken against any party found committing open burning in accordance with existing legal provisions.
"The public is urged to report any open burning activities to the Department of Environment (DoE) via its hotline at 1-800-88-2727 or through the eAduan JAS application," she said, adding that fire emergencies requiring immediate action can be directed to 999 or the Malaysian Fire and Rescue Department hotline at 1-800-88-994.
Jamaliah added that public health remains the state government's top priority during unhealthy API periods.
She said the Selangor Disaster Management Committee is prepared to channel face mask supplies to District Disaster Management Committees for distribution to public servants and the public, prioritising areas with the highest API readings.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Iran establishes 'economic war headquarters' amid US conflict, sanctions
Article:
ISTANBUL: Iran's Economy Ministry has established an "economic war headquarters" to coordinate and accelerate responses to economic problems arising from wartime conditions, Deputy Economy Minister Morteza Zamanian said Sunday.
Zamanian told the Tasnim news agency that the body would initially focus on issues falling within the ministry's responsibilities and authorities,  Anadolu Ajansi reported.
He said it would seek to quickly address war-related problems affecting businesses, trade, financing and other areas of the economy.
For issues extending beyond the ministry's authority, Zamanian said the ministry would use its role in broader economic policymaking, including through the government's economic commission and economic headquarters, to coordinate among institutions and pursue solutions at higher levels.
The main function of the new body is to centrally identify disruptions caused by wartime conditions and develop practical solutions, he said.
Zamanian added that the mechanism is intended to prevent issues requiring cooperation among several government agencies from becoming stalled by bureaucracy.
Measures being pursued include tax and customs support, banking facilities and financial instruments for businesses affected by the conflict, he said.
The move comes amid an ongoing conflict that began when the US and Israel launched strikes on Iran in February, followed by Iranian retaliatory attacks against US targets across the region.
Iran and the US signed a memorandum of understanding in June, mediated by Pakistan and Qatar, outlining steps toward ending hostilities, reopening the Strait of Hormuz and addressing economic restrictions.
Teheran has accused Washington of failing to fulfill its commitments under the memorandum, including sanctions relief and the release of frozen Iranian assets.
Washington, for its part, has accused Teheran of failing to meet its obligations and has maintained economic pressure on Iran, arguing that sanctions are aimed at restricting revenue and financial networks that it says support Teheran's military and regional activities.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Ministry to assist MACC probe, act against Baja 3 supplier, says Mat Sabu
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The Agriculture and Food Security Ministry will take action against the supplier of Additional Paddy Compound Fertiliser 3 (Baja 3) after it failed to meet its delivery commitments, said its minister Datuk Seri Mohamad Sabu.
He said the supplier's failure had caused delays in the delivery of fertiliser to padi farmers in the Muda Agricultural Development Authority (Mada) area.
"Based on the records, the supplier failed to fulfil the delivery commitments that had been set, resulting in delays in supplies to padi farmers.
"This failure not only affected the padi farmers, but also had a negative impact on the image of the ministry and the Madani government," he said in a statement.
Mohamad, who is also known as Mat Sabu, said he welcomed Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim's
directive for the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC)
to scrutinise the delays in the supply of Baja 3 in the Mada area.
He said the ministry would provide full cooperation to MACC to ensure all issues surrounding the supply process were properly clarified.
"I welcome the Prime Minister's directive for MACC to scrutinise the issue of delays in the supply of Baja 3 in the Mada area.
"In my view, this matter needs to be investigated transparently and thoroughly. The ministry will provide full cooperation to MACC to ensure that every question relating to the supply process can be clarified," he said.
Mohamad said the ministry would take the necessary action against the supplier in accordance with existing regulations and the terms of the contract.
He said the ministry's immediate priority was to ensure the remaining supply of Baja 3 reached affected padi farmers as soon as possible.
"At the same time, my priority and that of the ministry is to ensure that the remaining supply of Baja 3 can be distributed to the padi farmers immediately," he said.
He said monitoring of the distribution process would also be tightened to prevent similar delays from recurring.
"Monitoring will also be tightened so that problems like this do not recur in future," he said.
On Aug 27, Mohamad had said that the service contract of Taveekun Manufacturing Sdn Bhd for the supply of Baja 3 had been terminated following the delays.
He had said that Malaysian NPK Fertilizer Sdn Bhd, a subsidiary of Pertubuhan Peladang Kebangsaan (Nafas), had been appointed to take over the remaining supply to affected farmers.
Mohamad had said delivery of the remaining Baja 3 would begin on Sept 3, with the entire process targeted for completion within 10 days. He also instructed Mada to closely monitor the deliveries until the fertiliser reached the affected farmers.
On Aug 13, Malaysian Padi Farmers Brotherhood Organisation (Pesawah) chairman Abdul Rashid Yob was reported to have said that about 40,000 of the 60,000 padi farmers in the Mada area had yet to receive the additional fertiliser, raising concerns that the delays could affect this season's padi yields.
He had said that Baja 3 was needed when padi entered the reproductive stage, between 40 and 60 days after planting, to support panicle formation and grain filling.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Monaco probes top lawyer amid long-running property corruption scandal
Article:
MONACO: A top lawyer and senior adviser to Monaco's Prince Albert II was brought before a judge on Saturday amid a lengthy probe by investigators into a long-running scandal involving corruption and influence-peddling.
Lawyer Thierry Lacoste, a former school friend and adviser to Albert, was taken into police custody on Wednesday as officials investigate a massive property project that fell through, the Monaco Public Prosecutor's Office said, reported German news agency dpa.
Lacoste was brought before the investigating judge after being questioned and two extensions of his detention.
The judge opened formal criminal proceedings against him on suspicion of forming a criminal organisation, actively bribing a national public official, passively exerting undue influence and money laundering.
He has been placed under judicial supervision, the office said.
Lacoste denies the allegations and is still presumed innocent.
He told the police that the accusations had been made by a property magnate "who is dissatisfied because he was not awarded certain property projects in the Principality of Monaco," his solicitor's office said in a statement.
The magnate is attempting to exploit the principality's justice system for his own benefit, the statement said.
Those who had fought against corruption for years and whom it had not been possible to silence were now being accused of "corruption or exerting undue influence."
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Rescued Malayan tiger Yong Choh released into Tasik Kenyir national park
Article:
KUALA TERENGGANU: A female Malayan tiger rescued from Kampung Choh in Sungai Siput, Perak, on July 22 has been released into its natural habitat at Terengganu National Park in Tasik Kenyir.
The Natural Resources and Environmental Sustainability Ministry said the tiger, named Yong Choh and estimated to be seven years old, underwent rehabilitation at the National Wildlife Rescue Centre (NWRC) in Sungkai, Perak.
The animal was declared healthy for release by the Department of Wildlife and National Parks Peninsular Malaysia (Perhilitan) following veterinary examinations, blood tests, and disease screening.
"Minister Datuk Seri Arthur Joseph Kurup officiated the Wildlife Transfer Barge and Release Ceremony at Terengganu National Park, Tasik Kenyir yesterday, as part of efforts to strengthen wildlife conservation and manage human-wildlife conflicts," the ministry said in a statement today.
The ministry said the programme would help restore wildlife populations in their natural habitats, enhance genetic diversity among released animals, and support the long-term conservation of threatened species.
Other wildlife released under the programme include black panthers, sambar deer, barking deer, pangolins, common palm civets, mouse deer, and greater mouse deer.
Elephants affected by human-wildlife conflicts have also been returned to the wild.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Anak Krakatau eruption leaves Indonesian worker stranded at KLIA
Article:
SEPANG: An Indonesian domestic worker's plans to return to Jakarta were disrupted after her flight was cancelled following the temporary closure of Soekarno-Hatta International Airport due to volcanic ash from the eruption of Anak Krakatau.
The disruption affected 209 flights and 22,798 passengers, according to reports.
Yati Rasta, 61, said she arrived at the airport as early as 6am today to catch her 11am flight to Jakarta.
However, she was later informed that the flight had been cancelled and her ticket rescheduled to a 7am flight tomorrow.
With no money to pay for accommodation, Yati said she had no choice but to spend the night at the airport.
"I live in Puchong, but I cannot return to my employer's house as they have gone back to their hometown in Kuantan, Pahang.
"The money I had was already sent to my family back home. I have no relatives in Malaysia. I am alone here," she told reporters at Kuala Lumpur International Airport (KLIA) Terminal 2 today.
Checks at Terminal 2 found that several AirAsia flights to Jakarta had been cancelled, including AK034, scheduled for 1.20pm; QZ025 at 3.25pm; AK0386 at 5.10pm; and QZ0209 at 6pm.
Ina Rahman, 49, from Bangsar, said her two children were scheduled to fly to Jakarta at 11.30am today on an AirAsia flight before they were informed of the cancellation.
"At the moment, the only option is a flight tomorrow at around 8am or 9am, but even that is not certain," she said.
KLIA advised passengers travelling to Jakarta on affected flights to contact their respective airlines for the latest updates following the temporary closure of Soekarno-Hatta International Airport.
In a travel advisory, KLIA said the closure was prompted by volcanic ash from the eruption of Anak Krakatau detected in the vicinity of the airport.
KLIA also said several rest areas had been made available for affected passengers while they awaited further information on their flights.
At Terminal 1, the designated rest areas are at the observation deck on Level 5 of the Main Terminal Building, the CRS area on Level 3 of the Main Terminal Building and Gate C36 on the Mezzanine Level of the Satellite Building.
At Terminal 2, passengers can use the rest area at Level 3A, the Mezzanine Level of the Departure Hall.
Anak Krakatau, located in the Sunda Strait between Java and Sumatra, continued to erupt on Saturday, with authorities reporting lava ejections accompanied by tremors and booming sounds detected from observation posts.
The eruption began at 11.07pm Indonesian time on Friday and continued during observations conducted between midnight and 6am on Saturday.
Indonesia's Centre for Volcanology and Geological Hazard Mitigation said the volcano remained at Level III, or Alert, with authorities maintaining a three-kilometre exclusion zone around its active crater.
Authorities also said the newly formed structure of Anak Krakatau remained relatively small and was not considered capable of collapsing on a scale that could trigger a tsunami.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: UiTM duathlon: 9 participants experience breathing difficulties, 1 dies
Article:
KUANTAN: Nine Komander Kesatria Endurance Challenge (KKEC) participants, including a 21-year-old male student who died yesterday, experienced breathing difficulties during the duathlon event on Sept 4.
The student, Fadhlan Fakhry Solana Mohd Fellimal, 21, died at the intensive care unit (ICU) of Sultan Haji Ahmad Shah Hospital (Hoshas) in Temerloh at 2.08pm yesterday.
Maran police chief Superintendent Wong Kim Wai said two students remained admitted to Hoshas' ICU, while six others were receiving treatment at Jengka Hospital. All were reported to be in stable condition.
He said investigations found that the nine students — five men and four women — experienced breathing difficulties while participating in the event at the Universiti Teknologi Mara (UiTM) Jengka campus at 9.57pm. They were subsequently taken to Jengka Hospital for treatment.
"A male student from UiTM Seremban, Negri Sembilan, was in critical condition after suffering a severe drop in oxygen levels and was referred to Hoshas. He died while receiving treatment at the hospital's ICU yesterday.
"The Temerloh police headquarters operations room was alerted to the student's death by Hoshas at 5.50pm yesterday before informing the Maran police operations room," he said in a statement today.
Wong said a post-mortem was conducted at the Hoshas forensic unit late yesterday, with the results pending laboratory analysis.
Meanwhile, Wong said
two participants
were admitted to Hoshas' ICU yesterday after experiencing a drop in oxygen levels and were currently in stable condition.
"Six students are receiving treatment at Jengka Hospital. They are stable and remain under observation," he said.
Wong said investigations found that the UiTM Pahang Jengka campus was hosting the KKEC duathlon, which involved 521 participants from UiTM branches nationwide, except Sarawak.
The multi-sport endurance competition comprises an 8km run, a 20km cycling event and the 10km team endurance Mara Lasak event.
Fadhlan Fakhry, who represented UiTM Negri Sembilan at the event, was a final-year diploma student at its Seremban campus.
His father, who claimed his remains at Hoshas today, said Fadhlan Fakhry had participated in the previous two editions of the KKEC and
was in good health
before taking part in this year's event.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Six, including family of four, feared missing during Gunung Gerah hike
Article:
GUA MUSANG: Six people, including a family of four, are feared missing after joining the Trans Gerah Expedition at Gunung Gerah in the Lojing Permanent Forest Reserve here.
The group, comprising a married couple, their two children, and two mountain guides, began their trek on Aug 29.
They were expected to arrive at Pos Kemar in Perak on Thursday, but have remained unreachable.
A source said the last contact with one of the hikers was on the morning of Sept 1, when the family reported that they were safe and healthy.
"However, they could not be contacted after that, prompting a police report to be lodged over concerns for their safety," the source said.
District police chief Superintendent Sik Choon Foo confirmed receiving the report.
"We received a report on the incident and are in touch with other agencies, including the Forestry Department.
"The group has likely crossed the Kelantan border towards Pos Kemar," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Malaysia, Indonesia strengthen intelligence-sharing to combat cross-border drug syndicates
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia and Indonesia are strengthening intelligence-sharing and joint enforcement efforts as drug syndicates increasingly operate across borders and employ more complex methods to evade the authorities.
The matter was among the key issues discussed at the 14th bilateral meeting between Bukit Aman Narcotics Crime Investigation Department (NCID) and the Indonesian National Police's Directorate of Narcotics Crime (Dittipidnarkoba), Bareskrim Polri, held in Genting Highlands from Sept 2 to 4.
NCID director Datuk Hussein Omar Khan chaired the Malaysian delegation, while the Indonesian delegation was led by Dittipidnarkoba director Brigadier-General Eko Hadi Santoso.
Hussein said the meeting provided both sides with an opportunity to share their experiences in tackling drug trafficking and compare notes on syndicates with links to Malaysia and Indonesia.
"We also renewed our commitment to intelligence-sharing between both sides.
"Both Malaysia and Indonesia acknowledge the importance of working closely together and sharing information, especially when dealing with syndicates whose activities cross our borders.
"Drug syndicates do not operate within the boundaries of one country, so close cooperation and the swift exchange of intelligence are important in allowing us to take action against them," he said.
Hussein said both sides also shared updates on the investigation involving the Malaysian airline second officer arrested at Soekarno-Hatta International Airport on July 29.
"We shared the progress of the co-pilot case with our Indonesian counterparts and also expressed our appreciation for their swift action and the sharing of information with us.
"This case is an example of why cooperation between enforcement agencies from both countries is important. Information obtained and shared between both sides has allowed us to further develop our investigations," he said.
Police said the bilateral meeting also focused on strategic issues and the latest developments in regional drug trafficking, including the exchange of information on emerging trends and syndicate modus operandi.
Both sides discussed strengthening cooperation in operations and investigations, as well as efforts to dismantle increasingly complex and dynamic cross-border drug distribution networks.
The meeting comes amid continued cooperation between Malaysian and Indonesian narcotics authorities in tackling syndicates operating between the
two countries
.
Most recently, an NCID team was sent to Jakarta from Aug 11 to 15 to assist investigations into the
Malaysian second officer
arrested at Soekarno-Hatta International Airport.
Information obtained during the team's visit subsequently led NCID to arrest six local men, aged between 23 and 50, in Malaysia between Aug 20 and 28.
Hussein had said the six were believed to have supplied and transported drugs for the 39-year-old second officer and played "upline" and "downline" roles in the distribution network.
The bilateral meeting also sought to strengthen institutional ties between NCID and Dittipidnarkoba, with a welcoming dinner held on Sept 2 and a gala dinner the following day.
Malaysia's delegation included NCID deputy directors Deputy Commissioner Mohd Zani Che Din and Senior Assistant Commissioner Datuk Zairulnizam Mohd Zainuddin @ Hilmi, as well as senior intelligence, operations, investigation and international liaison officers.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Fadhlina praises Taanusiya for championing education, advocacy
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Education Minister Datuk Seri Fadhlina Sidek has praised Taanusiya Chetty for championing education and advocacy after the Malaysian beauty queen finished third at the Miss World 2026 pageant.
"I am impressed not only by her achievement on the world stage, but also by Taanusiya's commitment to making education and advocacy part of her cause.
"Beauty may open the door to the stage, but knowledge and critical thinking determine what we do once we are on it.
"Congratulations, Taanusiya. Continue to use the platform and voice you have to champion meaningful causes. Malaysia is proud!" she said in a Facebook post today.
At the pageant's final ceremony in Nha Trang, Vietnam, last night, Joheirry Mola Dominguez of the Dominican Republic was crowned Miss World 2026, while Spain's Elisabeth Reynes Alabern finished second.
Taanusiya, 26, secured a top-three finish after delivering consistent performances throughout the nearly month-long competition, overcoming 110 contestants from around the world.
Her achievement matches that of Lina Teoh, who also finished third at Miss World 1998, making them Malaysia's best-performing contestants in the history of the pageant.
Taanusiya, better known as Taanu, secured a spot in the Top Six after winning the Beauty With A Purpose (BWAP) segment, one of the pageant's major recognitions for contestants' commitment to and impact on community projects.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Malaysians stranded in Jakarta as Anak Krakatau eruption grounds flights
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The eruption of Mount Anak Krakatau, which spewed volcanic ash across parts of Indonesia, has disrupted flight operations, particularly at Soekarno-Hatta International Airport in Tangerang, Banten.
Several passengers, including Malaysians, shared their experiences online after being stranded while attempting to return home.
Among them was Threads user Spritzerphilips, who was stuck at the airport when her scheduled flight was affected today.
"I'm stranded in Indonesia and can't get back to Malaysia. I asked the Malaysian Embassy here in Jakarta for help, but they said there was nothing they could do.
"I'm trying to find a hotel, but many are already fully booked," she said.
An hour later, Spritzerphilips said she managed to secure a new flight on Tuesday.
"I've found a hotel and my flight has also been rescheduled for Tuesday. If it's still cancelled on Tuesday, I'll travel to Yogyakarta, as suggested by people on Threads. At least I can make alternative plans if I get stranded again," she said.
Other social media users suggested she travel by land to Yogyakarta or Surabaya to catch a flight back to Kuala Lumpur International Airport (KLIA).
Meanwhile, Facebook user Muhamad Norshahrizal Norizan said he and his family had been stranded in Jakarta for two days following repeated flight cancellations.
"Our flight has been cancelled for two days, including today. Please pray that everything goes smoothly for all of us," he said.
Another Facebook user, Musfyrah Mansor, was similarly stranded after her morning flight was cancelled.
She said the airline informed passengers that flights would be rescheduled once operations returned to normal.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: 'Unsustainable burden': PPP calls for urgent solution to public hospital doctor shortage
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The government must urgently address the chronic shortage of doctors, medical officers (MOs) and specialists in government hospitals, the People's Progressive Party (PPP) said.
Its president, Datuk Dr Loga Bala Mohan, said manpower shortages and the uneven distribution of healthcare personnel were contributing to excessive workloads, longer waiting times, burnout and delays in specialist treatment, with Sabah and Sarawak facing particularly serious challenges.
"This has been a pressing issue for many years, yet a permanent and comprehensive solution remains necessary.
"Delays in addressing the problem will not only affect patients but will also place an unsustainable burden on doctors, MOs, nurses and other healthcare personnel," he told reporters after chairing the party's Supreme Council meeting at its headquarters today.
He said the government must accelerate the abolition of the contract system, provide sufficient permanent positions, fill vacant posts, increase specialist training capacity and address the uneven distribution of doctors.
"We also called for the publication of updated manpower data on approved posts, filled positions and vacancies for doctors, MOs, specialists, nurses and other critical healthcare personnel."
He said PPP continued to receive complaints and appeals from members of the public experiencing delays in obtaining treatment at government healthcare facilities.
"While every case must be assessed individually, the wider manpower shortage is clearly one of the factors contributing to excessive waiting times and pressure on the system."
Citing a report from July last year, Loga Bala said doctors at understaffed facilities were seeing 80 to 100 patients a day, while some patients waited up to 6 hours.
More recently, he said a cancer treatment centre reportedly required 45 to 50 MOs but had only about half that number. On some days, 4 MOs were seeing up to 90 patients at its day-care facility.
"This is extremely worrying, particularly when Malaysia is facing a growing cancer burden and patients require timely diagnosis, treatment and follow-up care.
"The time for another temporary solution has passed. Malaysia needs a permanent, properly funded and sustainable solution to its healthcare manpower crisis," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Heavy traffic builds on major highways as holidaymakers head home
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Traffic volume has increased on several major expressways nationwide as holidaymakers make their way home following the school holidays.
The Malaysian Highway Authority's (MHA) Traffic Management Centre (TMC) said traffic was moving slowly along several stretches of the North-South Expressway (NSE), New Klang Valley Expressway (NKVE) and Kuala Lumpur-Karak Expressway as of 2.55pm today.
On the northbound NSE, slow-moving traffic was reported from the Senawang lay-by towards Port Dickson, Bangi to Kajang, and after the Sungai Besi toll plaza towards the city centre.
Southbound traffic was also moving slowly from Seberang Jaya to Juru, Gopeng to Tapah, Ayer Keroh to Jasin, and Sedenak to Kulai.
On the NKVE, motorists heading south faced slower traffic after the Damansara toll plaza towards Kayu Ara and the Sprint Highway.
Traffic was also reported to be slow westbound on the Kuala Lumpur-Karak Expressway from Bentong to Lentang and from the Gombak lay-by towards the Gombak toll plaza.
On the North-South Expressway Central Link (Elite), northbound traffic was slow from Putrajaya towards Bandar Saujana Putra.
In Johor, southbound traffic on the Malaysia-Singapore Second Link was moving slowly from the Gelang Patah rest and service area towards the Sultan Abu Bakar Customs, Immigration and Quarantine Complex.
The MHA also reported congestion on several expressways around the Klang Valley.
On the Damansara-Puchong Expressway (LDP), northbound traffic was slow from Puchong Utama to Puchong Intan, Taman Perindustrian Puchong to IOI Puchong, and Taman Megah to Damansara Utama.
Southbound traffic on the LDP was also moving slowly from Bandar Utama towards Taman Tun Dr Ismail.
Other affected stretches included Taman Suntex towards the General Operations Force base on the Cheras-Kajang Expressway; Serdang Lama towards KTM Serdang on the Besraya Expressway; and westbound traffic from Universiti Tenaga Nasional towards Putrajaya and the South Klang Valley Expressway on the Kajang Dispersal Link Expressway (SILK).
The MHA said weather conditions were good when the traffic update was issued.
Motorists have been advised to keep abreast of the latest traffic conditions when planning their journeys.
