Title: Japan releases tips on bear spray use amid concern over attacks
Article:
TOKYO: The Japanese government recently released guidelines on how to check the specifications of bear repellent sprays and properly choose and use them amid a proliferation of ineffective products on the market, Kyodo News reported.
With public interest in bear sprays growing as the country faces an increase in bear sightings and attacks, the Environment Ministry and the Consumer Affairs Agency have urged manufacturers and distributors to provide information on the efficacy of their products.
Unlike the United States, Japan has no uniform standards for such sprays.
According to the ministry and other sources, the main component in a repellent is capsaicin, the active chemical compound in chilli peppers.
The concentration of the ingredient in the product should be around 1 to 2 per cent, while the spray should have a range of at least 7.5 metres and a continuous spray duration of at least six seconds, according to the ministry's guidance.
"Some products rebranded for bears were actually made for use against people," said Shinjiro Sasaki, a ministry official who also recommended that people practice using the repellents.
The recently released warnings also urged people not to carry bear sprays unless necessary, to purchase products with a safety latch and to store them out of reach of children.
There were more than 50,000 bear encounters in the year ended March, a record high and double the year-earlier level, according to government data.
"Using the repellent sprays should be a last resort," Environment Minister Hirotaka Ishihara said at a press conference.
"We ask people to also take other countermeasures such as moving in large groups."
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: At flood-destroyed China-Nepal border, no sign of a once-busy port
Article:
ABOUT 20 Chinese rescue workers in bright orange operated excavators, shovels and ground-penetrating radar detectors on Sunday in an effort to find hundreds of people missing since a tsunami-like mudslide destroyed China's main border crossing with Nepal.
The Gyirong border crossing separating China's Tibet and Nepal became a grisly emblem of the devastation that followed the collapse of a glacier on the Nepal side of the border on Aug 26.
Reuters and other news agencies visited the land port, which sits in a narrow river gorge, in the first trip organised for foreign media by China's foreign ministry.
There was no trace of the five-storey Chinese customs building that had stood at the border before the disaster, video and pictures from the scene showed.
The only structure still visible from before the mudslide was a portion of a nearby water tower installation.
Workers had placed a Chinese flag at the spot where the border gate, at nearly 20-meters-tall, once stood.
Behind hazard signs that read "Danger Area Pass Quickly", three groups of about 20 rescue and recovery workers dug the earth using shovels while several red excavators stood by on Sunday afternoon.
Rescue workers have divided the search area into seven zones, officials told Reuters. They have completed searches in four of them, with three remaining.
[[nid:1526942]]
The mudslide has killed more than 1,300 people on both sides of the border, with more than 5,000 missing.
On Saturday, emergency crews in Nepal rescued a Chinese worker who had been in a tunnel linked to a hydropower station.
On China's side of the border, 31 people had been confirmed dead while 531 others were still classified as missing as of Friday.
Among those still unaccounted for are 261 foreigners from 23 countries, Chinese officials have said.
Gyirong County sits at an average altitude of more than 4,000 meters, though the port itself lies lower, at around 1,800 meters.
The risk of landslides, poor weather and deep mud has further complicated rescue and recovery efforts.
The only land route into Gyirong was restored by Wednesday morning, allowing China to bring in heavy equipment to aid recovery and eventual rebuilding.
State media has shown workers restoring power to the area by sinking temporary electric poles to reconnect it to the grid.
[[nid:1526941]]
Gyirong has emerged as the main border crossing for travelers and trade between Nepal and Tibet over the past decade, after a 2015 earthquake in Nepal badly damaged an alternative crossing farther east.
The port was shut down between July last year and January because of an earlier glacial flood.
In addition to a shipment point to Nepal for Chinese goods, including electric cars, it had also become a crossing point for thousands of Hindu pilgrims in recent years.
Many Hindus travel through Nepal to Mount Kailash, a high-altitude site in Tibet revered by Hindus and Buddhists. Hindus believe it to be the eternal home of Lord Shiva and his wife Parvati.
Many of the foreign nationals still missing in Tibet were pilgrims with extended families in India, diplomats in Beijing have said.
There are 49 Indian citizens among the missing.
* The writers are from Reuters
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Police step up highway monitoring as motorists return home after school holidays
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Police are closely monitoring major highways nationwide as motorists begin making their way home following the school holidays.
Bukit Aman Traffic Enforcement and Investigation Department (TEID) director Datuk Seri Mohammed Hasbullah Ali said highway patrol units were on the ground monitoring traffic conditions and ensuring the safety of road users.
He said police expected an increase in the number of vehicles on major highways as families returned home ahead of the resumption of school and work.
"Our highway patrol units are on the ground and we are monitoring the situation, particularly along the major highways.
"We urge motorists to plan their journeys properly, remain patient and, most importantly, obey traffic regulations throughout their journey," he told the New Straits Times today.
Hasbullah reminded motorists not to rush despite potentially heavier traffic and longer travelling times.
He said drivers should ensure they were sufficiently rested before embarking on long-distance journeys and stop at a safe location to rest if they began feeling tired or sleepy.
"Do not force yourself to continue driving when you are tired. Fatigue can affect your concentration and reaction time.
"Motorists should also avoid speeding, tailgating or making dangerous lane changes simply to save a few minutes on their journey," he said.
Hasbullah also reminded motorists not to use mobile phones while driving, stressing that their attention should remain on the road at all times.
He advised motorists to check their vehicles before travelling, particularly the tyres, brakes, lights and other essential components, to reduce the risk of breakdowns or accidents.
Motorists, he added, should wear their seat belts, while motorcyclists and pillion riders must use properly fastened helmets.
He also urged road users to exercise patience in congested areas and refrain from misusing the emergency lane.
"Give way to ambulances, police, fire and rescue vehicles and other emergency vehicles when necessary," he said.
Hasbullah said motorists should also maintain a safe following distance, use their indicators before changing lanes and observe speed limits.
He urged road users to take extra precautions during bad weather, including reducing their speed and increasing the distance between their vehicles and the one ahead.
"Everyone wants to reach home safely. There is no need to rush or take unnecessary risks.
"Be courteous to other road users, follow the rules and make safety your priority throughout the journey," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Komuniti Madani must be stronger bridge between government and people, says Wan Azizah
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The Komuniti Madani initiative should play a greater role as a bridge between the government and the people, Bandar Tun Razak member of Parliament Datuk Seri Dr Wan Azizah Wan Ismail said.
She said this role was crucial to ensure that every government policy and initiative reached its intended targets, while also effectively channelling public feedback to the relevant agencies for further action.
"Do not merely be information transmitters; be attentive listeners to the issues affecting the elderly, families in distress and the needs of the youth," she said at the Komuniti Madani appointment certificate ceremony for the Bandar Tun Razak parliamentary constituency here today.
Also present were the Prime Minister's political secretary Datuk Azman Abidin, Kuala Lumpur and Putrajaya Federal Territories Information Department director Normaizatulakmal Tujad, and Bandar Tun Razak Komuniti Madani chairman Jonathan Vela.
The Prime Minister's wife said that as the government's eyes and ears, community members must be proactive in following up on issues faced by the public.
She said while Komuniti Madani might not be able to resolve every issue raised, the network must ensure that each concern reached those with the authority and responsibility to act.
Meanwhile, she said the initiative must also serve as a frontline defence against the spread of false information, particularly in the age of social media.
"Misinformation spreads rapidly and can disrupt harmony. Komuniti Madani must be the first line of defence against falsehoods, adhering to the principle: 'Check before sharing'.
"We may have differing views, but we must always maintain mutual respect," she said.
Dr Wan Azizah said the true strength of any community lay in the relationships between neighbours and the willingness of people of diverse races and backgrounds to help and support one another.
In this regard, Dr Wan Azizah said the appointees must uphold trust and integrity, proactively engage with the community and listen closely to the people's concerns.
At the ceremony, Dr Wan Azizah also presented the Komuniti Madani Ambassador Award to Azizi Anas and S. Yugan, as well as appointment certificates to representatives from six sub-zones within Bandar Tun Razak.
Komuniti Madani is a rebranding of the 1,878 Komuniti Keluarga Malaysia groups following the launch of the Malaysia Madani framework on Jan 19, 2023.
In the Federal Territories of Kuala Lumpur and Putrajaya, 72 Komuniti Madani groups have been established, with the network's strength depending on volunteers who dedicate their time and energy to serving the community.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Gua Musang police: Six hikers feared missing after entering forest via Lojing and not emerging in Perak
Article:
KOTA BHARU, Sept 6 — Six individuals — four family members and two mountain guides — who entered a forest area through Pos Dakoh, Lojing, Gua Musang on August 29 are feared missing after not leaving at Pos Kemar, Perak as scheduled on September 3.
Gua Musang district police chief Supt Sik Choon Foo said family members of the hikers lodged a police report in Selangor today after they failed to return from their hike on the set date, adding that checks with the Forestry Department showed that the last contact with the group revealed that they were in the forest area in Perak.
“For now, we are dealing with the Perak authorities to secure confirmation as based on their last contact, they were in Perak and no longer in Kelantan,” he said when contacted today, adding that the group had permits to enter the forest and engaged the services of two mountain guides.
“We haven’t conducted an operation in Kelantan as checks revealed they crossed the state’s borders. We are preparing if there are developments or confirmation that they are in the Kelantan area,” he said.
The police are also checking information about the vehicle used by the group, including the possibility they used rental vehicles or transport arranged by the mountain guides. — Bernama

Title: Police confirm shooting of wanted drug suspect in Seremban housing area
Article:
SEREMBAN, Sept 6 — Police confirmed a local man suspected of drug-related activities was shot dead in a residential area in Garden Homes here early this afternoon.
Negeri Sembilan police chief Datuk Alzafny Ahmad said the incident occurred at 1.50pm. Further details will be disclosed by the Bukit Aman Narcotics Crime Investigation Department director at the Seremban District Police Headquarters tomorrow.
“Yes, I confirm the incident,” he told reporters here today.
The suspect, believed to be in his 50s, had eight previous records for drug and criminal offences. He was also wanted in connection with a case under the Kidnapping Act.
A resident, who only wanted to be known as Ali, 72, said he was at home after prayers when a neighbour informed him about the incident.
He said the neighbour reported hearing what sounded like several gunshots, though he did not hear them himself as he was indoors.
“After that, I saw many patrol cars and the road leading to the scene was cordoned off with police tape, with vehicles barred from entering.
“This is the first time such an incident has occurred in this residential area. We are concerned about our safety should a similar incident happen again,” he said.
The senior citizen added that about a week ago, residents noticed several suspicious cars parked near the area at midnight. — Bernama

Title: Don’t be deceived by RM2,500 deposit scam involving unofficial Kampung Jelutong SPK house offers, warns Jepak rep
Article:
BINTULU, Sept 6 — The public have been warned against falling victim to unofficial offers to purchase houses in the Kampung Jelutong Village Expansion Scheme (SPK) in Jepak.
Jepak assemblyman Iskandar Turkee said he had been informed about certain parties offering housing units in the area through unofficial channels, with prospective buyers reportedly being asked to pay a RM2,500 deposit.
He added the parties allegedly used registration forms and location maps to convince prospective buyers that the offers were genuine.
“I urge members of the public not to be easily deceived by such offers. For your own safety, do not make any payments, submit personal documents, or provide sensitive information before verifying the offer with the relevant authorities,” he said in a statement.
Handout photo shows one of the two housing models available at the Kampung Jelutong SPK. — Handout pic via The Borneo Post
Iskandar stressed that the public should first obtain official confirmation before taking any action or making payments in connection with housing offers there.
“Those who have received such offers or possess information related to the matter can contact ASP Douglas of the Commercial Crime Investigation Division, Bintulu district police headquarters at 019-812 9892 for verification and further information,” he said.
He also urged the public to remain vigilant and cooperate with the authorities to help curb scams and prevent others from falling victim.
The housing project is implemented by the Bintulu Development Authority, and as of April 30 this year, a total of 111 units have been completed. — The Borneo Post

Title: Selangor ready to distribute face masks in worst‑hit haze areas, with priority for vulnerable groups, says exco
Article:
SHAH ALAM, Sept 6 — The Selangor Disaster Management Committee is ready to distribute face masks to the public and civil servants to cope with the ongoing haze situation.
State Public Health and Environment Committee chairman Jamaliah Jamaluddin said the distribution would focus on areas recording the highest Air Pollutant Index (API) readings in Selangor, particularly targeting vulnerable groups.
“This action serves as an additional protective measure against the impact of current haze exposure,” she said in a statement today.
Meanwhile, she advised the public, especially high-risk groups such as senior citizens and individuals with heart or respiratory conditions, to limit physical and outdoor activities when API readings reach unhealthy levels.
“The public is also advised to reduce strenuous outdoor activities and remain indoors if air quality is unhealthy, while staying updated on the latest API readings in their respective areas,” she added.
Jamaliah said the state government would continue to monitor the situation closely and take necessary measures to safeguard public health, safety and well-being.
“The state government will keep obtaining technical data and updates from relevant agencies, including the Department of Environment and the Malaysian Meteorological Department, to help determine appropriate action should air quality deteriorate further.
“The public is also urged not to engage in activities that could worsen air quality and to comply with advisories and directives issued by the authorities,” she added.
Six areas in Selangor recorded unhealthy API readings as at 4 pm today, namely Johan Setia (181), Shah Alam (168), Kuala Selangor (158), Petaling Jaya (157), Klang (156) and Banting (155). — Bernama

Title: Seven UiTM students remain under treatment after heat‑related incident; outdoor endurance events called off
Article:
SHAH ALAM, Sept 6 — Seven Universiti Teknologi MARA (UiTM) students are still receiving treatment and undergoing medical monitoring following a heat-related incident while taking part in an endurance event in Pahang on Friday.
In a statement today, UiTM vice-chancellor Prof Datuk Shahrin Sahib @ Sahibuddin said the university management was paying particular attention to the health and welfare of all the affected students, who are being treated at Sultan Haji Ahmad Shah Hospital (HOSHAS) in Temerloh and Jengka Hospital.
“Based on the latest information from HOSHAS, Liya Zafirah Muhammad from the Perak branch remains under treatment in the intensive care unit (ICU), while Meor Aqil Wildan from the Perlis branch is also under close monitoring at the same hospital.
“The five other students at Jengka Hospital are Nur Nabihah Musyidah Md Nasri (Johor branch, Segamat Campus), Nur Alia Farhana Abdul Fattah (Pahang branch, Jengka Campus), Muhamad Adam Azfar Suzaini and Muhammad Anas Shahrul Nizat from the Johor branch, as well as Izzharith Zafran Muhammad Zulkarnain from the Pahang branch,” he said.
He said UiTM would continue to maintain close communication with the hospitals and the families involved to provide the latest updates on their health.
Following the incident, Shahrin said the university administration had decided to cancel all Komander Kesatria Endurance Challenge (KKEC) 2026 competitions involving outdoor activities that were scheduled to take place today.
He said the university was also giving its full cooperation to the authorities to assist with any investigation into the incident, while conducting a comprehensive assessment of safety procedures, health screening, risk management and emergency response measures for the programme.
“All forms of support, including logistics, transportation and management assistance, have also been fully mobilised to ease the burden on the victims’ families,” he said.
Shahrin said the university management had instructed UiTM deputy vice-chancellor (Student Affairs) Prof Mohd Sazili Shahibi to be on the ground to directly monitor the welfare of the affected students.
He said the university’s top management, together with UiTM Pahang branch Rector Prof Dr Azhan Hashim @ Ismail, had also paid their last respects to the student who died in the incident.
Shahrin urged the public to respect the privacy of the students’ families and refrain from spreading unverified information.
A 21-year-old KKEC 2026 participant from UiTM Negeri Sembilan, Seremban Campus, Fadhlan Fakhry Solana Mohd Fellimal, was reported to have collapsed while taking part in the event on Sept 4.
He was subsequently treated in the ICU at HOSHAS and was pronounced dead at about 2 pm yesterday.
Fadhlan Fakhry Solana, the second of four siblings, was buried at the Elmina Muslim Cemetery in Denai Alam today. — Bernama

Title: Hunting team records nine crocodiles captured in four‑day Kuala Baram operation
Article:
MIRI, Sept 6 — The crocodile-hunting team ‘Eric Cat’ has recorded the capture of nine reptiles throughout their four-day operation in Kuala Baram, which kicked off on September 2.
Team spokesman Eric Chong Fook Shin said the last catch was made last night, which was a 14-foot (over 4 metres) crocodile.
“Of the nine crocodiles, five were male while the remaining four were female,” he said in a statement.
Chong said the 14-foot crocodile was the team’s largest catch during their Kuala Baram operation.
He added that the team would take a two-day break before continuing its next operation at Sungai Teru in Baram. — The Borneo Post

Title: Zulkifli: Higher allocations show Madani govt commitment as Malaysia earns global Islamic recognition
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 6 — The Madani Government remains committed to strengthening Islamic affairs in Malaysia through increased funding and efforts that have helped the country achieve global recognition in several areas.
Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Religious Affairs) Dr Zulkifli Hasan said the increase in allocation for Islamic affairs from RM1.5 billion in 2023 to RM2.6 billion this year reflected the government’s commitment to advancing the sector.
“Malaysia’s haj management has been recognised as the best in the world for five consecutive years, while the country’s halal industry is ranked number one globally,” he said when officiating the Madani Kita Programme (PMK) 2026 at the Lembah Pantai Community Centre here today.
He also noted that Malaysia’s Islamic banking sector has held the top global position for the past 10 years.
Zulkifli said the government would continue developing the Islamic affairs agenda within the framework of the law while upholding respect for diversity and differences in society
The PMK programme, an initiative by the Department of Islamic Development Malaysia (JAKIM) and agencies under Religious Affairs, aims to bring government services closer to the people through information-sharing, engagement and various community services.
The programme offers various services, including advice, health screenings, education, training and career development. — Bernama

Title: Don’t link salvation in the hereafter to politics, says religious affairs minister
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 6 — Differences in political support should not lead to a punitive or condescending attitude towards others, let alone linking salvation in the hereafter to membership of or support for any political organisation.
Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Religious Affairs) Dr Zulkifli Hasan said the determination of heaven and hell is the absolute right of Allah SWT and cannot be guaranteed by any individual, leader or political organisation.
He said support for any political organisation was not a measure of attaining the pleasure of Allah SWT, as faith, piety and righteous deeds based on the Quran and Sunnah served as the primary foundations.
“The attitude of claiming one’s group is definitively pure while others are excluded from the mercy of Allah SWT is a form of self-praise and ghuluw (extremism), which is strictly prohibited in Islam,” he said in a Facebook post.
Zulkifli said political parties were merely wasilah or intermediaries in human endeavours that were not exempt from weaknesses and ijtihad (independent reasoning), and could not be equated with religion or used as an absolute measure of a person’s standing before Allah SWT.
In this regard, he urged all parties to mature their political culture by making justice, the well-being of the ummah (Muslim community) and good character the core principles, rather than exploiting religious sentiments for political gain.
“Engage in mature and ethical politics based on justice and the well-being of the ummah, without compromising the values of faith and ukhuwah Islamiah (Islamic brotherhood),” he said, while asking society to distinguish between religion as a guide to life and political parties as platforms for human endeavour.
The statement was made in response to media reports yesterday quoting PAS secretary-general Datuk Seri Takiyuddin Hassan as saying that supporting PAS and its Islamic-based struggles could be a path to heaven.
Takiyuddin was reported as saying that those who joined PAS and fought for Islam had the opportunity to earn the reward of heaven, in addition to describing those who died defending Islam as martyrs. — Bernama

Title: Sri Aman only area with very unhealthy API reading of 216 as of 4pm, with no hazardous readings nationwide
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 6 — No area recorded a hazardous Air Pollutant Index (API) reading due to the haze as of 4 pm today, although Sri Aman in Sarawak was the only area to record a very unhealthy reading of 216.
The Air Pollutant Index Management System (APIMS) portal reported unhealthy API readings in 35 other areas nationwide, moderate readings in 27 areas and good readings in four areas.
Sarawak remained the worst-hit state, with 11 areas recording unhealthy air quality, namely Samalaju (196), Samarahan (196), Kuching (191), Bintulu (190), Mukah (188), Sarikei (185), IPD Serian (182), ILP Miri (176), Sibu (174), Miri (170) and Limbang (157).
Kapit was the only station in the state to record a moderate API reading, at 90.
Meanwhile, six areas in Selangor — Johan Setia (181), Shah Alam (168), Kuala Selangor (158), Petaling Jaya (157), Klang (156) and Banting (155) — as well as Batu Muda (164) and Cheras (162) in Kuala Lumpur; Putrajaya (162) and Labuan (157) also recorded unhealthy API readings.
Other areas with unhealthy API readings include Jerantut (168) and Temerloh (161) in Pahang; Nilai (167), Seremban (164) and Port Dickson (121) in Negeri Sembilan; Kota Kinabalu (157) and Kimanis (151) in Sabah; as well as Tanjung Malim (153) in Perak.
In the southern region, unhealthy air quality was also recorded in Segamat (159), Tangkak (151), Batu Pahat (127) and Kluang (103) in Johor; as well as Alor Gajah (154) and Bukit Rambai (154) in Melaka.
An API reading of 0 to 50 indicates good air quality; 51 to 100 moderate; 101 to 200 unhealthy; 201 to 300 very unhealthy; and 300 and above hazardous. — Bernama

Title: Doctors induce coma for Batu Pahat toddler wounded in stray dog attack
Article:
JOHOR BAHRU, Sept 6 — A two-year-old girl is fighting for her life after being critically injured by a pack of five stray dogs outside her grandmother’s house in Kampung Tambak, Sungai Kelambu, Peserai in Batu Pahat yesterday.
Nur Haira Watikah Mohammad Hamizi, suffered severe head and facial injuries in the 7am attack, The New Straits Times reported.
Her grandmother, Darlinda Darlis, 56, told the newspaper that the girl was in her care while her parents were at work in Johor Baru.
Darlinda said she found the front door open after taking a bath and saw the dogs attacking the girl outside the house.
Her son helped rescue the bloodied child before they rushed her to Sultanah Nora Ismail Hospital in Batu Pahat, where she was treated in the red zone and placed in an induced coma.
The girl was later transferred to Sultanah Aminah Hospital here because of the severity of her injuries, Darlinda  said.
The grandmother claimed the dogs had been abandoned by hunters who used them to hunt wild boar in a nearby oil palm plantation, adding that residents had long been concerned about their growing numbers.
Batu Pahat district police chief Assistant Commissioner Shahrulanuar Mushaddat Abdullah Sani confirmed a police report had been lodged and said the case was being investigated under the Child Act 2001.

Title: Budget 2027 to emphasise support for M40 and lower‑income groups, says Finance Minister’s aide
Article:
LUMUT, Sept 6 — Budget 2027 is expected to place particular emphasis on efforts to address socioeconomic issues, including the welfare of the middle-income (M40) and lower-income groups, according to an aide of the Finance Minister.
Muhammad Kamil Abdul Munim, who is political secretary to Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim, said the focus on both groups was necessary as they are among those most affected by economic pressures and current cost-of-living challenges.
“The Budget to be announced by the Prime Minister will be another more inclusive Budget, one that is closer to the people and can, to some extent, resolve several problems and issues that have arisen.
“For now, the parties involved are still conducting direct engagement sessions with all stakeholders to finalise the Budget,” he said.
He said this when met after officiating the National Khatam Keris Traditional Ceremony organised by the Perak branch of the Persatuan Silat Seni Gayong Malaysia and the Silat Anak-Anak Gayong Perak Gathering at Teluk Batik Campsite here today.
Anwar, who is Prime Minister and Finance Minister, is scheduled to table Budget 2027 in the Dewan Rakyat on October 9.
Muhammad Kamil said existing initiatives such as the Sumbangan Tunai Rahmah (STR) and Sumbangan Asas Rahmah (SARA) would continue to be strengthened to ease the financial burden on households.
“Assistance programmes such as STR and SARA will continue, and we await further announcements by the Finance Minister,” he said.
Muhammad Kamil said consideration was also being given to proposals to improve existing initiatives and introduce other forms of financial support to ease the burden on middle-income households.
“The government’s priorities also remain focused on ensuring that political and economic stability remains strong to guarantee the smooth implementation of national policies,” he said. — Bernama

Title: Anwar and old friend Al Gore reunite (virtually) to talk climate challenges, decades after ‘reformasi’
Article:
SERDANG, Sept 6 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim today said he spoke with former US vice-president Al Gore about the global climate crisis, haze affecting Malaysia and the country’s transition towards cleaner energy.
Anwar said Gore, who was in Singapore, had expressed sympathy over the haze after the Air Pollutant Index (API) reading in Serian, Sarawak exceeded 500 two days ago.
“Former US vice-president Al Gore was in Singapore, and I had the opportunity to have a lengthy discussion with him about the environment and what is now referred to as the climate crisis,” he said in his speech at the closing ceremony of the Malaysia Agriculture, Horticulture and Agrotourism Exhibition here today.
Anwar said they also discussed the wider effects of climate change, including the recent floods in Nepal.
“Glacier ice from the Himalayan mountain range, which had remained firmly intact for thousands of years, melted into a massive valley in Nepal.
“This affects not only the people of Nepal, but also the people of Malaysia,” he said.
He said their discussion also touched on Malaysia’s commitment and ongoing efforts to accelerate the country’s energy transition away from fossil fuels towards cleaner and more sustainable energy sources.
“These are matters we cannot afford to forget; however, what we are capable of planning, we must execute,” Anwar said.
He also invited Gore to visit Malaysia soon to continue their discussions and explore closer cooperation on climate change and the country’s energy transition.
Gore, a prominent climate campaigner and founder and chairman of The Climate Reality Project, served as US vice-president from 1993 to 2001.
Anwar and Gore’s association dates back to 1998, when the American was US vice-president and Anwar was deputy prime minister before his dismissal from government and subsequent arrest.
During the 1998 Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit in Kuala Lumpur, Gore publicly praised Malaysia’s
reformasi
movement, which had emerged following Anwar’s removal from office, prompting an angry response from the government of then-prime minister Tun Dr Mahathir Mohamad.
Separately, Anwar said he had declined an opportunity to meet former Indonesian president Joko Widodo, who is currently in Penang, due to his prior commitments in Kuala Lumpur today.

Title: Fadhlina praises Taanusiya’s Miss World showing and her commitment to education advocacy
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 6 — Education Minister Datuk Seri Fadhlina Sidek has praised Taanusiya Chetty, who finished third in the Miss World 2026 pageant, for championing education and advocacy as part of her cause.
“I am impressed not only by her achievement on the world stage, but also by Taanusiya’s commitment to making education and advocacy part of her cause.
“Beauty may open the door to the stage, but knowledge and critical thinking determine what we do once we are on it.
“Congratulations, Taanusiya. Continue to use the platform and voice you have to champion meaningful causes. Malaysia is proud!” she said in a Facebook post today.
In last night’s ceremony in Nha Trang, Vietnam, Joheirry Mola Dominguez of the Dominican Republic was crowned Miss World 2026, while Elisabeth Reynes Alabern of Spain finished second.
Taanusiya, 26, finished among the top three after delivering impressive and consistent performances throughout the nearly month-long competition, overcoming the challenge of 110 other contestants from around the world.
The achievement matches the record set by Lina Teoh, who also finished third at Miss World 1998, making the two Malaysian representatives the country’s best-performing contestants in the history of the contest.
Taanusiya, better known as Taanu, qualified for the Top Six after winning the Beauty With A Purpose (BWAP) segment, one of the major Miss World recognitions, awarded based on the contestants’ commitment to and impact of the community projects they champion. — Bernama

Title: Youth and Sports Ministry to prioritise grassroots sports development and athlete welfare in Budget 2027
Article:
GEORGE TOWN, Sept 6 — The Youth and Sports Ministry (KBS) has submitted an initial framework of its Budget 2027 proposals to the Finance Ministry (MOF) for consideration, with grassroots sports development, youth participation and athletes’ welfare among the ministry’s priorities.
Youth and Sports Minister Dr Mohammed Taufiq Johari said the framework was prepared based on input gathered through the Madani Youth Budget Tour being conducted in six zones nationwide.
“Although all the tour sessions have not been completed, KBS has obtained various views from youth organisations, sports associations as well as unorganised youths for review and assessment.
“So far, we have held initial discussions with Finance Minister II Datuk Seri Amir Hamzah Azizan and have submitted the initial framework for MOF’s assessment,” he told reporters after attending the Oregeon Tower Run Series flag off at The TOP Atrium, here today.
The ministry wants to provide more space and opportunities for the public to participate in sports activities, particularly at the grassroots level to produce more reserve athletes and will focus on athletes’ welfare, including those who have retired or had previously contributed to the country, he added.
Dr Mohammed Taufiq said his ministry also takes into account the views of sports associations and youth organisations as well as the needs of youths in rural areas and those who have not previously participated in any ministry organisations or programmes.
He also shared that his ministry intends to hold various nationwide tour programmes in 2027 to reach as many youths as possible, including through large-scale activities and smaller programmes at the community level.
“We want to implement programmes touring throughout Malaysia next year to meet as many young people as possible by carrying out mass activities as well as small-scale activities so that we can engage with every young person,” he said. — Bernama

Title: Anak Krakatau chaos strands Malaysians in Jakarta, with hotels full and next flights two days away
Article:
JAKARTA, Sept 6 — Malaysians stranded in Jakarta after volcanic ash from the eruption of Mount Anak Krakatau disrupted flights are now scrambling for alternative arrangements, with some travellers facing delays of several days before they can return home.
One traveller who goes by the moniker Spritzerphilips on Threads was a picture of fatigue and anxiety after being stranded at Soekarno-Hatta International Airport after her flight, scheduled for today, was cancelled.
“Stranded in Indonesia, can’t get back to Malaysia, asked for help from the embassy here but they said they couldn’t help either,” she wrote.
About an hour later, Spritzerphilips said she managed to secure a new flight for Tuesday.
“Hotel is sorted, ticket has also been rescheduled to Tuesday,” she wrote,, adding that she would consider travelling by land to Yogyakarta if the new flight was cancelled.
Other Threads users suggested travelling overland to Yogyakarta or Surabaya to catch a flight to Kuala Lumpur.
Another Malaysian traveller, Muhamad Norshahrizal Norizan, said on Facebook that he and his family had been stranded in Jakarta for two days after their flights were repeatedly cancelled.
“My family and I are stranded, our flight has been cancelled for two days already... today is the same,” he posted.
Facebooker Musfyrah Mansor also said she was stranded at the same airport after her flight was cancelled this morning.
She said her airline had informed passengers that flights would be rescheduled once conditions had returned to normal.
The disruption follows the eruption of Mount Anak Krakatau, which sent volcanic ash into the airspace around Jakarta and forced Soekarno-Hatta International Airport to suspend operations today.
The airport closure disrupted 209 flights and affected 22,798 passengers, according to Indonesia’s Civil Aviation Director General Lukman F Laisa.
Malaysia Airlines and Batik Air have cancelled a combined 20 Malaysia-Jakarta flights today, while AirAsia has cancelled or rescheduled a number of services.
The situation remains fluid as Indonesian authorities monitor the spread of volcanic ash and its impact on flight operations.

Title: Water supply to 34,000 accounts in Machang expected to be restored tomorrow after pipe repairs
Article:
MACHANG, Sept 6 — Water supply to about 34,000 consumer accounts in Machang, southern Kota Bharu and parts of Pasir Puteh is expected to be restored in stages from noon tomorrow following a main pipe leak in Pulai Chondong here.
Kelantan Public Works, Infrastructure, Water and Rural Development Committee chairman Datuk Dr Izani Husin said the leak in the 1,100-millimetre glass-fibre reinforced plastic (GRP) pipe was detected on Friday, with excavation and repair works beginning on the same day.
He said the pipe, which was commissioned in 2018, had a leak measuring about 10 centimetres, while cracks affecting almost half of the pipe were also detected and believed to have been caused by erosion.
“Air Kelantan Sdn Bhd (AKSB) instructed specialist contractors from Kemaman, Terengganu to carry out urgent repairs, which were initially expected to take 10 days but were completed within four days,” he told reporters after inspecting the repair works here today.
Following the disruption, he said 24 lorries and water tankers have been deployed to supply about 1.04 million litres of water a day to affected consumers, including hospitals, dialysis centres, prisons, schools, hostels, educational institutions and residential areas, with assistance from water operators in Kedah, Pahang, Johor, Penang, Selangor and Perak.
Meanwhile, AKSB head of Production Dr Mohd Hilmi P. Ramli said the company planned to replace the GRP pipe with mild steel pipes following the fourth leak since it was commissioned eight years ago.
He said that, in the initial phase, about 800 metres of the 10-kilometre pipeline would be replaced with funding from Pengurusan Aset Air Berhad, at an estimated cost of RM3 million. — Bernama

Title: FT mufti: ‘Religious exploitation’ more accurate term, not ‘riding on religion’, to describe misuse
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 6 — The term ‘religious exploitation’ is more appropriate and objective than ‘riding on religion’ to describe the act of misusing religion for worldly interests, said Federal Territories Mufti Ahmad Fauwaz Fadzil.
He said the term ‘riding on religion’ should not be used indiscriminately as it could lead to generalisations about religious figures, including scholars and preachers who sincerely champion the cause of Islam.
The term ‘religious exploitation’ focuses more specifically on the act of misusing religion to gain wealth, influence or position, while also more clearly illustrating the existence of those who take advantage and those who are deceived.
“On the other hand, the term ‘riding’ has a negative and harsh connotation and tends to carry elements of sarcasm and personal accusations against the perpetrator.
“The term ‘religious exploitation’ more accurately describes the power structure in this phenomenon, namely the existence of those who take advantage (exploit) and those who are exploited (members of the public who are deceived or misled), in line with the actual meaning of the evidence from the Quran and Sunnah,” he said in the Tinta Mufti column published by the Federal Territories Mufti Department today.
Ahmad Fauwaz said the exploitation of religion was prohibited and condemned in the Quran, including through verses in Surah At-Taubah and Surah Al-Baqarah, both of which illustrate forms of religious exploitation that occur when religion is manipulated as a tool to obtain wealth and worldly interests, an act that is reprehensible as it exploits the name of Allah for personal gain.
He said the Prophet Muhammad also warned against those who use religion to deceive people for worldly interests, as narrated by al-Tirmidhi, which means: “At the end of time, a group of men will emerge who deceive people by using religion to obtain worldly gains... their tongues are sweeter than sweets, while their hearts are the hearts of wolves.”
Ahmad Fauwaz said the hadith described individuals who present themselves as knowledgeable and pious to gain the trust of the community, while using religion as a guise to obtain money, influence or position.
In this regard, he advised the public not to be easily deceived by outward appearances, but instead to conduct proper checks before placing their trust, wealth or obedience in any individual who uses religion as a tool for personal gain.
At the same time, he reminded those involved in preaching, religious knowledge and religious work to always maintain sincerity and fulfil their responsibilities solely for the sake of Allah and to attain His pleasure. — Bernama

Title: More money for Agriculture Ministry? Anwar says maybe — if the books stay clean, so farmers won’t suffer
Article:
SERDANG, Sept 6 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim today said the Ministry of Agriculture and Food Security could receive a bigger allocation in Budget 2027, provided the ministry continues to uphold good governance.
His remarks came after its minister Datuk Seri Mohamad Sabu called for an additional allocation during the closing ceremony of the Malaysia Agriculture, Horticulture and Agrotourism Exhibition here.
Anwar, who is also finance minister, said additional funding could be considered as long as the ministry ensured that public money was managed properly and reached farmers, fishermen and paddy planters.
“Because large expenditures must be managed well, and we have no choice.
“If we want to safeguard the fate of farmers, paddy planters, and traders, we must ensure good management.
“Allocations may increase, but if there are leakages and misappropriation, those who suffer are the farmers, fishermen, and paddy planters,” he said.
Speaking to reporters later, Mohamad who is better known as Mat Sabu, said the additional allocation is to allow his ministry to prepare early for potential challenges next year.
He said this includes measures to deal with the El Niño phenomenon, which is expected to continue into early next year.
The ministry also needs to be prepared for a possible spike in fertiliser prices amid ongoing geopolitical tensions, he said.
“Our secretary-general has already mapped out our requirements and early measures, particularly if temperatures surge.
“Aquaculture will take a hit. We’re looking at potential fish loss and similar issues. So we must have aid ready to deploy.
“And that’s just one scenario out of many. Say there’s a sudden surge in fertiliser prices; we then need to ask the government for financial support as well,” Mohamad said.
He said the request is essentially for supplementary funds, and that it can be adjusted according to how conditions develop later.
The government will table Budget 2027 when the Dewan Rakyat sits again next month.

Title: Kedah appeals for continued cloud seeding as Pedu, Muda and Ahning dam levels keep falling
Article:
ALOR SETAR, Sept 6 — The Kedah state government appealed for the continuation of cloud seeding operations, coordinated by the National Disaster Management Agency (NADMA), to help raise declining water levels at dams in the state.
State Public Works, Natural Resources, Water Supply, Water Resources and Environment Committee chairman Datuk Mohamad Yusoff Zakaria said that while the operation carried out from Thursday to yesterday resulted in rain, it was still insufficient to boost reservoir levels.
He said before cloud seeding on Sept 2, total water supply at the Pedu, Muda and Ahning Dams stood at 37.14 per cent, but had dropped to 36.64 per cent this morning.
“The water level at Pedu Dam is now at 38.46 per cent, compared to 39.02 per cent on Sept 2, while Muda Dam recorded 9.04 per cent, down from 9.32 per cent previously,” he told Bernama today.
Meanwhile, supply at Ahning Dam stood at 45.00 per cent, compared to 45.32 per cent over the same period.
He said sufficient dam water supply is critical to ensure the smooth operation of padi irrigation systems, as Kedah’s agricultural sector is heavily dependent on these water sources.
Earlier, the federal government took early and targeted measures to address dry weather conditions, low rainfall, and the risk of deteriorating air quality through cloud seeding operations in Kedah and Perlis. — Bernama

Title: Bukit Lagi Hindu temple row: Perlis police get two more days to detain activist as probe widens into criminal trespass
Article:
KANGAR, Sept 6 — The remand of a 55-year-old activist detained over social media posts linked to a gathering concerning the demolition of a Hindu temple in Bukit Lagi has been extended by two days as police pursue a separate criminal trespass investigation.
Magistrate Ana Rozana Mohd Nor allowed the police application today for the extension, with the activist being investigated under Section 447 of the Penal Code, Harian Metro reported today.
Kangar district police chief Assistant Commissioner Yusharifuddin Mohd Yusop confirmed with the Malay newspaper that the suspect would remain in custody until tomorrow to assist investigations into the alleged criminal trespass.
The activist was initially remanded for two days from September 5 to assist investigations into allegedly inciting social media posts related to the organisation of a gathering over the demolition of the Sri Veera Maha Kaliamman Kovil temple in Bukit Lagi.
He was arrested in Petaling Jaya, Selangor last Thursday following 15 police reports lodged between August 22 and 27 over posts made through his TikTok account.
The earlier investigation is being conducted under Section 4(1) of the Sedition Act 1948 and Section 233 of the Communications and Multimedia Act 1998.
Police had said the posts included a picture promoting the Perhimpunan Merah Maha Kali gathering, which was held at the temple site on August 30.
The temple was demolished by the authorities on August 20, with police previously saying the gathering was believed to have been organised in response to dissatisfaction over the demolition.
Police had also warned that the gathering could potentially trigger racial and religious tensions in Perlis.

Title: Fadhlina pledges no SJKT closures as RM12.6m Sungai Bakap Tamil school project gets going after 17 years
Article:
NIBONG TEBAL, Sept 6 — The government has assured that no Tamil vernacular school will be closed as construction finally begins on a RM12.6 million replacement building for SJKT Sungai Bakap after nearly 17 years of delays.
Education Minister Fadhlina Sidek said the Madani Government would instead continue to focus on the development and maintenance of all SJKT, as well as programmes to strengthen teachers and pupils.
She said the assurance was necessary as there were still perceptions in the community that some SJKT could be shut down.
“We give an assurance that, under the Madani Government, no SJKT will be closed.
“Instead, we will focus on all schools in terms of development, maintenance and programmes related to strengthening teachers and pupils,” she said.
Fadhlina was speaking to reporters after witnessing the groundbreaking and handover of the letter of acceptance for the new SJKT Sungai Bakap building here today.
The RM12.6 million project, to be carried out by Yayasan Didik Negara and monitored by the Penang Education Department, is expected to be completed within 56 weeks.
The new school will be built at a site about 2km from the existing location and will comprise six classrooms, special-purpose rooms and other facilities.
Fadhlina, who is also Nibong Tebal MP, said the new building was important in providing better and more comprehensive educational facilities for children in the Sungai Bakap area.
She also apologised to parents, pupils and teachers for the long wait before the project could finally be realised.
The project had been delayed since 2009 due to implementation issues, financial constraints and legal disputes, according to Bernama.
Penang special committee chairman for Tamil schools Datuk Seri S. Sundarajoo said the existing school building, which houses more than 100 pupils, was in a dilapidated condition.
He said the project had previously faced issues involving land, contractor delays and court proceedings before these were resolved.
Sundarajoo, who is also the state housing and environment executive councillor, said the state government was targeting the construction of three SJKT buildings this year.
He said SJKT Sungai Bakap was the second to be developed, while work on SJKT Juru was expected to begin before the end of the year.

Title: Volcanic ash grounds 20 Malaysia-Jakarta flights by Malaysia Airlines, Batik Air
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 6 — Malaysia Airlines and Batik Air have cancelled a total of 20 flights between Malaysia and Jakarta today after volcanic ash from the ongoing eruption of Mount Anak Krakatau disrupted operations at Jakarta’s Soekarno-Hatta International Airport (CGK).
Malaysia Airlines said in its post on X that it would cancel 12 flights between Kuala Lumpur (KUL) and Jakarta (CGK), namely MH713, MH712, MH711, MH710, MH717, MH716, MH721, MH720, MH723, MH722, MH725 and MH724.
“Given the evolving situation, Malaysia Airlines is closely monitoring developments.
“Further updates on affected flights will be communicated directly to affected customers,” it said.
The national carrier reminded passengers to ensure their contact details are up to date via “My Booking” on its website to receive timely updates by email and SMS.
Customers may also contact its Live Chat support on the Malaysia Airlines website or its Global Contact Centre for assistance.
“The safety of our passengers and crew remains our utmost priority,” it added.
Meanwhile, Batik Air said in a separate statement that it had cancelled eight scheduled flights between Malaysia and Jakarta today, namely OD398, OD399, OD346, OD347, OD388, OD389, OD390 and OD391.
Six of the cancelled services operate between Kuala Lumpur International Airport and Jakarta, while two operate between Subang and Jakarta.
It said the decision followed close coordination with aviation authorities and airport operators, reflecting its commitment to the safety and wellbeing of passengers and crew.
“The presence of volcanic ash in the airspace can reduce visibility, interfere with aircraft navigation systems, and potentially compromise engine performance,” it said.
Batik Air said it would continue to monitor the situation and provide updates on flight operations to and from the affected destinations through its official website and social media channels.
Affected passengers would also be notified through their registered contact details.
“Affected passengers may request to reschedule their travel to the next available Batik Air flight, subject to availability, or request a refund.
“Passengers are advised to contact Batik Air’s Customer Care Centre or their respective booking channels for assistance with their preferred option,” it said.
Batik Air, a Malaysian carrier, operates under Indonesia’s Lion Air Group. — Bernama

Title: United Sikhs Malaysia head into Nepal’s worst-hit flood zone to help 98 kids whose parents are missing (VIDEO)
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 6 — Five Malaysian volunteers are heading deep into one of Nepal’s worst-hit flood zones, travelling over rough terrain to deliver emergency supplies and help families whose homes and communities have been devastated by floods and landslides.
The team from United Sikhs Malaysia, a Malaysian humanitarian aid organisation involved in disaster relief and community assistance, is travelling to Dhunche in Rasuwa district to establish a base camp before pushing on to Syapru Besi near the Nepal-Tibet border.
In a Facebook post today, the group said that the journey to Dhunche is expected to take 10 to 12 hours, with the team then facing challenging off-road conditions to reach Syapru Besi, about 40km from the border.
The volunteers will first unload relief supplies at their base before continuing to the affected town.
The team’s immediate priority is to build temporary shelters for families displaced by the disaster, the group’s legal director Raspreet Kaur told the
The New Straits Times
.
She said a local resident had also sought help for 98 children whose parents remained missing, with the team planning to provide necessities including colouring materials.
The volunteers had earlier prepared mosquito nets and tarpaulins worth about RM28,000 for around 300 affected families, with the supplies delivered to a gurdwara in Kathmandu.
United Sikhs Malaysia said Team A is expected to remain in Nepal for about two weeks, while additional teams are on standby depending on the situation on the ground.
https://www.facebook.com/UNITEDSIKHSMALAYSIA/videos/06092026-mission-update-nepal-flood-reliefunited-sikhs-malaysias-team-a-is-curre/3827014714104717/
United Sikhs Malaysia’s mission comes as other Malaysian teams and organisations are also responding to the disaster.
Mercy Malaysia has deployed a humanitarian assessment team to Nepal to assess conditions on the ground and identify urgent needs, including emergency shelter, food, clean water, sanitation and healthcare.
Malaysia has also sent 11 officers and personnel from the Special Malaysia Disaster Assistance and Rescue Team (SMART) to assist with search-and-rescue operations in areas affected by the floods and landslides.
The 10-day SMART mission is expected to include operations in areas where people may still be trapped, while the team will also assist in efforts to locate Malaysians affected by the disaster.
The Malaysian government has also pledged US$1 million (RM4.2 million) to help Nepal’s disaster victims and support recovery efforts.
The disaster has particularly disrupted access to communities in Rasuwa, where flooding and landslides have damaged roads, bridges and other infrastructure, making relief operations difficult.

Title: Zahid tells parties to park PM talk, focus on Melaka polls instead
Article:
ISKANDAR PUTERI, Sept 6 — Barisan Nasional chairman Datuk Seri Ahmad Zahid Hamidi today urged political parties to put talk of who could become prime minister after the 16th general election aside for now, saying the focus should instead be on the upcoming Melaka state election.
The Umno president said it was too early to name or discuss a potential prime ministerial candidate when the timing of Parliament’s dissolution and the next general election remained unknown,
Harian Metro
reported.
“It is too early to put forward someone or a particular figure to hold that position because the election could still be far away or it could be otherwise.
“We do not know when Parliament will be dissolved. I think it is better that we put that aside for now and focus on facing the Melaka state election,” he was quoted as saying after the closing of the 2026 National Orang Asli Sports Carnival at the EduCity Sports Complex here.
Zahid, who is also deputy prime minister, said attention should remain on the Melaka election before any discussions on federal-level political matters take place.
On cooperation among political parties for the Melaka election, he said this would only be decided after the Melaka Legislative Assembly was dissolved.
His remarks came after PAS president Tan Sri Abdul Hadi Awang said the party had a potential prime ministerial candidate from among its leaders for GE16, but that it was not yet time to reveal the individual.
He made the remarks at  PAS’ annual congress in Kota Bharu, Kelantan last Friday.

Title: Sarawak extends cloud‑seeding operations to tackle transboundary haze as Serian API shows improving trend
Article:
KUCHING, Sept 6 — Cloud seeding operations across Sarawak have been extended until tomorrow in an ongoing effort to mitigate transboundary haze affecting the state.
Sarawak Disaster Management Committee (SDMC) chairman Datuk Amar Douglas Uggah Embas said the extension followed a successful operation yesterday, which brought rainfall over the targeted Bakun and Murum Dam areas.
“Today’s operation will continue as planned and will be carried out where suitable cloud and weather conditions permit,” he said in a statement today.
Sarawak has been conducting cloud-seeding operations targeting key dams and water catchment areas in the state since Thursday.
Meanwhile, Uggah said air quality in the Serian district had shown an improving trend, with the Air Pollutant Index (API) reading at 185 as at noon today, placing it in the unhealthy category.
“There is a downward trend for the API level in Serian as we enter the second of three days of monitoring. The API is primarily affected by wind direction and the source of hotspots,” he said.
He said continued monitoring was necessary before any formal recommendation regarding Serian’s emergency status could be submitted to Sarawak Premier Tan Sri Abang Johari Tun Openg and Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim.
Uggah said data from the Asean Specialised Meteorological Centre (ASMC) revealed zero hotspots in Sarawak, while 184 hotspots were detected in neighbouring Kalimantan, Indonesia. — Bernama

Title: Chief Justice leads 128‑strong Terengganu honours list in conjunction with Sultan Mizan’s 64th birthday
Article:
KUALA TERENGGANU, Sept 6 — Chief Justice Tun Wan Ahmad Farid Wan Salleh topped the list of 128 recipients of the Terengganu state honours and medals in conjunction with the 64th birthday celebration of the Sultan of Terengganu, Sultan Mizan Zainal Abidin.
The Regent of Terengganu, Tengku Muhammad Ismail Sultan Mizan Zainal Abidin, graced the investiture ceremony held at the Balairong Seri of Istana Syarqiyyah here.
Also in attendance were his younger siblings, Tengku Seri Setia Mahkota Raja Tengku Datuk Seri Muhammad Muaz; Tengku Puteri Utama Raja Tengku Nadhirah Zahrah; and Tengku Puteri Daulath Raja Tengku Fatimatuz Zahra’.
Also present were Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Samsuri Mokhtar and members of the state government leadership.
Wan Ahmad Farid was conferred the Darjah Kebesaran Seri Setia Sultan Mizan Zainal Abidin Terengganu (S.S.M.Z), which carries the title Datuk Seri.
Also receiving the S.S.M.Z were Qatar Ambassador to Malaysia Datuk Seri Salah Mohammed Al-Sorour; Chief of Air Force General Tan Sri Muhamad Norazlan Aris; and Terengganu Equestrian Association deputy president Tan Sri Abdullah Taib.
Tengku Muhammad Ismail also conferred the Darjah Kebesaran Datuk Setia Sultan Mizan Abidin Terengganu (D.S.M.Z), which carries the title Datuk, on Federal Court Judge Datuk Che Mohd Ruzima Ghazali and CelcomDigi Berhad board adviser and former chief executive officer Datuk Mohamad Idham Nawawi.
Also receiving the D.S.M.Z were executive chairman of Mirmas Holding Sdn Bhd, Datuk Awalan Abdul Aziz and managing partner of Messrs Feroz@Co Datuk Feroz A S Moidunny.
In addition, 27 recipients were conferred the Darjah Kebesaran Datuk Paduka Mahkota Terengganu (D.PMT), which also carries the title Datuk, including renowned actor Datuk Abdul Manan Embong, better known as Eman Manan, and Terengganu Tourism, Culture, Environment and Climate Change Committee chairman Datuk Razali Idris.
Also receiving the same award were Dungun Member of Parliament Datuk Wan Hassan Mohd Ramli; former Universiti Malaysia Terengganu vice-chancellor Prof Datuk Dr Mohd Zamri Ibrahim; and Terengganu police chief Datuk Mohd Khairi Khairudin.
Tengku Muhammad Ismail also conferred the Darjah Kebesaran Setia Sultan Mizan Zainal Abidin Terengganu (S.M.Z) on 17 recipients, including Terengganu Information, Dakwah and Syariah Empowerment Committee chairman Muhammad Khalil Abdul Hadi.
At the ceremony, 17 recipients were awarded the Darjah Kebesaran Setia Mahkota Terengganu; 20 received the Darjah Kebesaran Ahli Sultan Mizan Zainal Abidin Terengganu; and 39 individuals were awarded the Darjah Kebesaran Ahli Mahkota Terengganu. — Bernama

Title: Two foreigners remanded for allegedly taking plant specimens without permission from Santubong National Park
Article:
KUCHING, Sept 6 — Two foreign nationals have been remanded for allegedly taking plant specimens without permission from Santubong National Park last Thursday.
Sarawak Forestry Corporation (SFC) said both individuals were remanded for three days, from September 4 to September 7, to assist with the investigation.
“On September 3 at around 1.50pm, the two individuals were checking out of the park after conducting an activity in the area. Following observations, they were suspected of taking and collecting plant specimens from the area.
“Inspections revealed four transparent plastic bags filled with plant specimens, believed to have been taken from the national park. Two backpacks and other items were also seized for further investigation,” SFC said in a statement
All specimens have been recorded and retained as case exhibits, and are currently undergoing identification and further examination to determine their type and species status.
SFC is working with the Royal Malaysia Police (PDRM) to complete the investigation and any subsequent action.
The investigation also takes into account the provisions under the National Parks & Nature Reserves Ordinance, 1998 [Cap. 27], which prohibits the taking or removal of plants from national park areas without permission from the controller of national parks and nature reserves.
Under Section 26 of the said Ordinance, no person is allowed to take or destroy plants within a national park, or to remove any plant, whether living or dead, without the controller’s permission
“SFC takes a serious view of any activity involving the taking, collecting, or removal of biological resources from Totally Protected Areas (TPAs) without permission. Such activities may impact the integrity of biodiversity and the long-term conservation efforts of Sarawak.
“Members of the public and visitors are reminded that all flora, fauna, and natural resources within national park areas are protected and must not be taken, removed, or carried out without valid authorisation,” SFC said. — The Borneo Post

Title: Former minister’s remand extended two days in Tabung Haji RCI hotel‑lease probe
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 6 — The remand of a former minister detained over investigations into a Lembaga Tabung Haji (TH) hotel‑lease issue in Saudi Arabia has been extended for two more days.
According to Bernama, Magistrate Muhammad Bukhori Md Ruslan Zakariah issued the extension, which runs from tomorrow until Tuesday, after the Malaysian Anti‑Corruption Commission (MACC) applied for it at the Putrajaya Magistrate’s Court this morning.
MACC Chief Commissioner Abd Halim Aman, when contacted, said the case is being investigated under Section 16(a)(A) of the MACC Act 2009.
The former minister was previously remanded for five days after being detained when he arrived to give a statement to MACC last Wednesday.
The Royal Commission of Inquiry (RCI) report on TH, released publicly on July 29, recorded weaknesses in TH’s management and operations between 2014 and 2020 and listed problematic investments requiring forensic audit.
The report also stated that suspicious transactions and concealment of information had occurred.

Title: Anwar expresses solidarity with Indonesia over volcanic disaster and haze challenges
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 6 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim today expressed solidarity with the people of Indonesia following the volcanic disaster and haze-related challenges currently facing the country.
Anwar said he conveyed this when he contacted former Indonesian President Joko Widodo, better known as Jokowi, who is currently in Penang to attend the Penang Peace Dialogue.
In a post on his Facebook page today, Anwar said the conversation also saw the two leaders exchange updates.
Anwar also apologised for being unable to meet Jokowi in person in Penang due to his previously scheduled programme with farmers, livestock breeders, smallholders and the agro community at the Malaysia Agriculture, Horticulture and Agrotourism Exhibition (MAHA) 2026.
“Malaysia and Indonesia are not merely neighbouring countries, but two kindred nations bound by history, culture and close ties of brotherhood.
“Positions and responsibilities may change hands, but friendship and mutual respect will endure,” he said, stressing that the ties would continue to be nurtured for the well-being of the people of both countries and the prosperity of the region.
According to a report by national news agency ANTARA, Jokowi attended the Penang Peace Dialogue held in George Town and shared his views on the role of leaders and the people in laying the foundations for peace at a gala dinner last night.
Jokowi is also scheduled to deliver a keynote address at the forum today. — Bernama

Title: DOE monitors bush and peatland fires in Mukah, Daro in Sarawak amid dry spell
Article:
KUCHING, Sept 6 — The Department of Environment (DoE) is paying special attention to the fire incidents reported in bushes and peatlands near Jalan Sibujaya Barat in Mukah and Sungai Nai in Daro amid the current dry spell.
DoE deputy director-general (Development) Azuri Azizah Saedon said based on the latest status, the fire in the Jalan Sibujaya Barat area had been mostly controlled, covering an area of nine hectares.
“However, the fire still affects approximately one hectare in the Jalan Sibujaya Barat area and is currently being extinguished,” she said in a statement on Sunday.
In Sungai Nai, Azuri said approximately 2.5 of the three hectares are still burning, but the situation is reported to be under control, according to the Fire and Rescue Services Department.
She said fires in vegetation and peatland have the potential to produce smoke and release pollutants that can affect local air quality if left unchecked.
As such, she said the DoE Sarawak will continue monitoring the latest status of the fires at the mentioned locations, including assessing the potential impact on air quality.
Drone flights will also be carried out to obtain the latest picture of the fire status and the extent of the affected area, she added.
“Air quality monitoring and follow-up actions will be carried out based on the actual situation on the ground and the results of the DoE assessment together with relevant agencies.”
Azuri said monitoring would be strengthened if there was an increase in air pollution, while appropriate actions would be taken in accordance with the existing legal provisions to minimise the impact of the fire on the environment and public health.
In the meantime, she reminded members of the public that open burning is an offence under the Environmental Quality (Amendment) Act 2024, which carries a fine ranging from RM25,000 to RM1,000,000, or imprisonment of up to five years, or both.
She said a compound of up to 50 per cent of the maximum fine may also be imposed for each offence.
Everyone is urged to report any fire or open burning to the Fire and Rescue Department at 999 or the DoE at 1-800-88-2727.
Meanwhile, Azuri said two air quality monitoring stations in Sarawak recorded very unhealthy Air Pollutant Index (API) readings as of 10am on Sunday. They were Kuching with an API of 223 and Sri Aman (215).
Ten of the 35 locations across the country that registered unhealthy API readings were in Sarawak. They were Samalaju (200), Bintulu (198), Mukah (194), Samarahan (192), Sarikei (188), Serian and Industrial Training Institute Miri (both 182), Sibu (181), Miri (175) and Limbang (160).
The remaining air quality monitoring stations with unhealthy API were Selangor (6), Johor (4), Sabah and Negeri Sembilan (3 each), Kuala Lumpur, Melaka and Pahang (2 each), Putrajaya, Terengganu and Labuan (1 each).
Based on the Asean Specialised Meteorological Centre (ASMC) report on Saturday, Azuri said a total of 184 hotspots were detected in Kalimantan, 373 in Sumatra and one in Perak.
“ASMC also reported moderate to thick transboundary smoke plumes observed covering the northern part of Borneo.
“Moderate to thick smoke plumes were also observed from hotspots detected in many areas of Kalimantan as well as central and southern Sumatra,” she said.
She added that moderate haze was also observed in Singapore and southern Peninsular Malaysia. — The Borneo Post
